title: Ask ERP manual
text: Plain-words notes for people who use the ERP. Ask ERP reads this file, the glossary and the other approved documents when it answers. If an answer is wrong or missing, fix it here and rebuild the knowledge file (node scripts/build-ask-knowledge.mjs).

title: What Ask ERP is
text: Ask ERP answers questions about how the ERP works and about the company's own figures. It answers only from the approved documents and from the screens you are allowed to see. It cannot change anything. It does not show pay, ID numbers, PINs or passwords. If it does not know, it says so. Ask one store and one period at a time for the best answers. Questions may be in English or Taglish.

title: Who sees what
text: Each person sees only the stores they are assigned to, and only the screens their role allows. A manager sees the reports for their own stores. Staff see their own screens. If Ask ERP says it cannot show something, the same screen is closed to you in the ERP: ask an admin if you think you need it. An admin can open a screen for one person, or for a whole position under Position access defaults (/admin/access-defaults).

title: Recording an expense
text: Open Expenses, then New expense (/expenses/new). Choose the store, the date, the supplier and the category, then the amount. An expense that is a bill to pay later is booked to accounts payable. An expense paid by a staff member out of their own pocket is a reimbursement (/expenses/reimbursements). Bills that repeat every month are set up under Recurring expenses (/expenses/recurring) and drafted for you. A budget cap on a category only warns; it never blocks an expense.

title: Cash requests
text: A cash request (/cash-requests) is money given out ahead of a purchase. It must be liquidated afterwards: the receipts are recorded and any change is returned. A cash request not liquidated for a long time shows up in Findings.

title: Suppliers and bills
text: Suppliers are under Accounts payable (/ap/suppliers). The bills still owed are on /ap. Everything the company still owes in one place (bills, loans, other obligations) is on /liabilities/unpaid. Wages are not part of what Ask ERP shows.

title: Reading the money: reports
text:
- Income Statement (/reports/income-statement): sales, cost of sales, expenses and profit for the dates you pick, for one store or all of yours. - Store Comparison (/reports/store-comparison): the income statement of several stores side by side. - Sales Rollup (/reports/sales-rollup): sales by day, month or store, and by channel (walk-in, Grab, Foodpanda). - Spending by Item (/reports/expense-items): where the expense money went, by group, category and item. This is the report to ask about cost drivers. - Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, Trial Balance, AP Aging and AR Aging are under Reports too. - Budgets (/budgets): the cap per category per period against what was actually spent.
A figure always belongs to a period and a store. When Ask ERP gives a figure it names both.

title: Stock
text: Stock on hand and the moves are under Inventory (/inventory). Low stock (/inventory/low-stock) lists the items at or below their threshold, worst shortage first. An item with no threshold set does not appear there; it shows as a finding so a manager sets one. Physical counts are at /inventory/counts and moves between rooms or stores at /inventory/transfers.

title: Cash, till and remittance
text: The till and its counts are at /till. Cash kept at a store that must be handed over to the office is tracked under Remittance (/remittance). A counted shortage on a closed shift is a finding until someone resolves it.

title: Sales days
text: Each store's sales for a day are recorded and verified under Sales days (/sales-days). A sales day that was changed after it was verified is flagged.

title: Findings
text: Findings (/findings) is the list of things the system noticed: books that do not tie, cash not remitted on time, unusual spending, a store with items that have no reorder threshold, and more. Unusual spending is checked per store: a category far above its usual week, one expense far above its usual, many more expenses than usual, a possible duplicate, an expense approved by the person who recorded it, and spending over a budget cap. These only warn; nothing is blocked. A finding stays on the list while it is still true. Accepting a finding for a while does not make it disappear from the count.

title: People and attendance
text: Staff, attendance and payroll have their own screens (/staff, /attendance, /payroll). Pay and personal details are private and are not available through Ask ERP.

title: Settings
text: Stores, access, business rules and the AI hub are under Settings (/settings). Only a super admin can use the AI hub, which holds the AI keys and the monthly spending cap. The number of questions one person may ask a day is also set there.

title: Glossary — what the words actually mean
text:
Living document. This exists because in this domain the obvious reading of a name is often wrong, and an agent that guesses writes confidently incorrect code. Add an entry the moment a term surprises you. That is the trigger — not "is this important", but "did I have to go read code to find out what this meant".
- The name lies. The obvious reading is wrong. Read before using
- Verified in code on the cited line
- Business usage, from Ian — not a code artefact
---

title: dineInSales
text:
Means: unlimited-package sales only. *Not* "all dine-in".
À la carte and online both fall into walkIn. ERP does not compute this field — it pulls it from POS. Consequence: it maps straight to account 4100 (dine-in, unlimited) with no reconstruction needed.

title: takeOutSales
text: A residual, not a measurement. Math.max(0, totalGross - dineInSales) (POS/src/app/api/external/sales/route.ts:53). It absorbs everything totalGross counts that dineInSales does not — today that is à la carte only, because no online orders exist yet. Never treat it as a revenue figure on its own; treat a non-zero value as a reconciliation signal.

title: deliverySales — means neither delivery NOR one consistent thing
text:
Two different meanings depending on which document wrote it (ERP-rebuild/src/lib/financial/sales-report/derive-totals.ts:88-96):
DAY doc - *"the full channel sum + branchDelta (i.e. it currently equals totalSales)"* — a duplicate of the total, not delivery
SHIFT doc - nonRemittedChannelsTotal = max(0, totalSales − remittedChannelsTotal) — the channels whose money never reaches the till (Foodpanda, Grab, …)
The day-doc behaviour is a known wart frozen in place — *"preserved verbatim so create and adjust agree."* Never read this field as delivery revenue. The useful concept underneath is non-remitted channels, which is what SalesChannel.isRemittedDaily decides.

title: dineInSales — ALSO means something different in the ERP than in POS
text: The entry above defines POS's meaning (unlimited-package sales). The ERP's sales-report form stores something else in the same field: *"Stored dineInSales — the remitted-daily channels"* (derive-totals.ts:83-85). One field name, two meanings, depending on which system wrote the row. Anything reconciling ERP against POS must know which it is holding.

title: cashPayments — a floored residual, not a measurement
text: *"cash is DERIVED: remitted channels − online − credit − other, floored at 0"* (derive-totals.ts). Flooring at zero hides a negative, and a negative here would be a real signal that the tender figures disagree. Same family as takeOutSales: a residual wearing a measurement's name.

title: creditCardPayments — always 0
text: *"Always 0 — card tenders are captured through the online accounts."* The field exists; nothing populates it. Do not build a card-tender breakdown on it.

title: sessionMode
text: Two values only: 'package_dinein' | 'alacarte'. Walk-in à la carte and in-store take-out are the same value — there is no take-out flag anywhere in POS. Online orders live in a separate onlineOrders collection and get sessionMode: 'alacarte' hardcoded onto a synthesised receipt. See DEF-004, DEF-005.

title: session
text: A group of diners at a table, from seating to payment. Not an auth session, not an HTTP session. When you mean authentication, say *auth session* explicitly.

title: shift day
text:
05:00 → 05:00 Manila. The attendance calendar, and not the financial business day, which is midnight-based. A closing staffer who punches out at 01:30 belongs to the shift day they *started* — so that one punch sits on the previous shift day and the current business day at the same time.
Two calendars, one repo. toShiftDay lives in packages/domain/src/attendance/shift-day.ts, toBusinessDate in packages/core/src/datetime.ts, and ShiftDay / BusinessDate are separate branded types so passing one where the other belongs does not compile. v1 made the same distinction and wrote down why it named the field sessionDate rather than dayKey (ERP-rebuild/src/lib/attendance/shift-day.ts:3-6).

title: punch
text: One raw credential presentation at a terminal — "this person presented this credential at this device at this time". A fact, never an outcome: a punch carries no hours, no lateness and no pay. Postgres adjudicates (bible §5.1). The direction the staffer pressed is stored as assertedIntent, and the name is the specification: the device asserts, the server decides.

title: attendance day
text:
The adjudicated result for one person on one shift day — hours, breaks, night differential, anomalies.
Never called a "session". session above already means *a group of diners at a table*, and packages/db/schema/sessions.ts already took the second meaning for auth. v1's attendanceSessions would be the third meaning of one word in one system.

title: receiptSeq
text:
An integer written by two different allocators from non-comparable sequence spaces — a server-arbitrated counter when online, a per-device daily counter when offline. Refunds write 0. It is not a per-store monotonic key, despite looking exactly like one. DEF-001, DEF-002.
---

title: Sales and service
text:
unli / unlimited / package - The core product: unlimited samgyupsal, fixed price per head, variable consumption. Its margin moves with *how much people eat*, which is why it gets its own revenue account (4100)
à la carte - Ordering individual items rather than the package. Sold both dine-in and take-out
take-out - Always items / à la carte — never unli. Includes delivery: *delivery is a mode of take-out, not a third channel*
refill - A repeat serving within an unli session. Cooldown 60s, anchored on SERVE not order, with two safety valves (10 min "still in kitchen", 20 min "first serving pending"). All magic numbers in app code today — DEF-021
addon - An extra item bought during a package session. Counted into dineInSales via dineInAddonSalesAmount
kitchen ticket - The kitchen's copy of an order. billOnServe: true means no bill line exists yet
billOnServe - The bill is created on SERVE, not on order. Recognise revenue at order instead and unserved orders become revenue. POS/src/lib/kitchen/customer-order-billing.ts
void - Cancels the *sale*. In POS a void is a status flip on the same document, not a reversing entry

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
refund - A separate negative receipt referencing a parent. Currently mints colliding numbers — DEF-001
re-ring - A corrected receipt replacing a voided one; consumes the retained void cash
voidCashRetained - Cash collected on a voided receipt and not refunded. It sits in the drawer backing no sale, so ERP carries it into expected remittance and books it to a suspense liability
comps - Complimentary items. Contra-revenue (4950), confirmed by Ian — not marketing expense
day feed (T-375) - The stored, immutable copy of one POS v1 response for one store-day (pos_v1_day_feeds): the exact text, its parsed form and a sha256. A sales day on a linked store is DERIVED from it and nothing else. Append-only: every fetch is a fact, none is edited or de-duplicated. Interim — retired per store at P2, when that store's sales reach Postgres directly (ADR-015)
linked store (T-375) - A store with a row in pos_v1_store_links. That row is the whole switch — no flag, no env var. Linked: its sales days are imported from POS and never typed. Unlinked: today's typed path, labelled "Typed — store not linked to POS"

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
unlinked store (T-382) - A store whose pos_v1_store_links row has unlinked_at set. It takes typed sales days again; days already imported from POS stay as they are (verified ones frozen by the 0185 lock, hardened by 0187). Its row keeps its POS id, so no other store can link that POS store. An admin can relink it (an UPDATE of the same row). "Linked" means a LIVE row
tender (master) (T-375) - A store's tender definition (tenders): a name, cash or wallet, the money account a wallet pays into, and how POS v1 spells it. Not sales_day_tenders, which is one day's wallet rows (where that day's money went). The master is what a till will sell against; sales_day_tenders is what a day recorded
payment option (T-629) - One of the ORG's master list (payment_options): Cash, GCash, Maya, QRPH, Credit card, Debit card. It owns the NAME and the KIND (cash or wallet). A store switches it on by holding a tenders row for it (so a tender IS the store's switch); tenders.name / tenders.kind are a mirror a trigger keeps equal to the option. Group company-wide by payment_option_id, never by tender name

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
platform sales (T-375) - Foodpanda, Grab and similar: typed per day on the store's NON-remitted channels, kept outside the figures POS derives. One removable seam, until platforms are rung through POS
wholesale (item flag) (T-443) - items.sellable_wholesale. Not "sold in bulk": it means the item may be sold to another store, a franchisee or an outside buyer (e.g. Xlice) — anyone who is not a diner. The commonest case is the commissary (Lipa) selling to the company's own branches. The word is kept in code and in soldAsLabel; screens say "Sold to other stores or buyers (wholesale)". v1 called the own-branch case commissary → branch sales (computeBranchPrice)
variation (item) (T-443) - An item grouped under a top-level parent through items.variant_of_item_id (Kimchi 250g under Kimchi). Each variation is a full item — own code, stock, price history — not a pack size of one pool (Ian, R-A). One level only; a variation has the same kind as its parent. Not purchase_unit (a buying container) and not parent_slab_item_id (slab to slices) and not menu_item_variants (the MENU side)

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text: store charge / charge_total / amountDue (T-627) - An extra peso amount a cashier adds to a bill for things outside the menu (leftover food, an extra griller). Not a service charge (none is charged) and not part of total: charges come AFTER discounts and VAT, outside the VAT base, never discounted, never in the senior/PWD base. On a receipt total = subtotal - discount_total still holds; charge_total sits beside it and amountDue (priceSession) = total + charge_total is what the customer pays. pos_day_closes.gross_total and the Z's grossTotal are what was BILLED (total + charges); the sales day books them as other_charges (4500), never service_charge

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
reservation deposit / deposit_applied / deposits_applied / account 2170 (T-628) - Money a customer paid ahead to hold a table. Not sales and not income when taken: it is a liability (2170 Customer deposits payable) until it is applied to the bill, refunded or kept by a manager (then 4500). Its balance is derived from the append-only events (taken - voided - applied - refunded - kept), never stored. pos_sales_receipts.deposit_applied is the part of a bill paid from it (a payment line "Deposit", not a tender row); sales_days.deposits_applied is the Z total, posted Dr 2170 by routeSalesDay as a tender of the sale. Taken / voided / refunded / kept post beside the Z of the till that moved the cash (pos_deposit entries), so the drawer matches the day the cash moved. A void is refused once applied; a cancelled or no-show reservation with money held cannot close until a manager refunds or keeps it, with a reason
refunds (sales day) (T-375) - sales_days.refunds: POS refunds of the day, contra-revenue 4950, on a feed-sourced day only. Never comps — comps keep their meaning (complimentary items). Derived as the amount by which POS's method totals exceed its paid total, above the rounding band

title: Money and books
text:
journal entry - The whole transaction: a header plus two or more lines that balance. In the legacy ERP an "entry" was a *single leg* with no header — the root defect (DEF-006)
leg / line - One account movement. v2 stores explicit debit / credit; v1 stored direction: in\ - out and derived the rest from an account-name prefix
nominal ledger - The revenue and expense accounts. The legacy system has none — the P&L is a hand-maintained scan list. Building one is the reason this project exists
control account - A summary account (AP, AR, Inventory) that a subsidiary ledger must reconcile to. The legacy system has none: ap{supplierId} *is* the account, so "AP total" is just a sum with nothing to check it against
posted vs draft - Draft is a worksheet; posted is a financial fact. Posted records are immutable — corrections are new reversing entries, never edits
reversal - A new, dated, opposite entry that unwinds a posted one. Not the same as a void, which cancels a document
contra-revenue - Reduces revenue rather than being an expense: discounts (4900), returns and comps (4950), loyalty points redeemed (4910)

title: Money and books (cont.)
text:
normal balance - Whether an account naturally carries a debit or credit. A declared column in v2 — never inferred from a code prefix, which is how the legacy system got it wrong
fiscal period - A dated window with status open / closed / locked. No posting into a closed period by any ordinary path, including crons and ETL. The one way in is the admin override (bible row 193): admin and super_admin only, a typed reason, an audit row, and the exemption dies with the transaction. The period stays closed; reopening is still not built
trial balance - The one-query check that total debits equal total credits. Must pass at any moment
legacy_code - The old system's account identifier, kept on the new account so migrated data can be traced back
management ledger - What this system is. Not a statutory filing basis. VAT here is a label; reported sales are not all sales. Never label or export output as BIR-ready — bible §13 row 75

title: Money and books (cont.)
text:
statutory payment (T-193) - Paying SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG or BIR what payroll withheld and owes (the credit postPayRun leaves in 2210-2240). Stored in statutory_payments (+ statutory_payment_lines, one per store); what is owed is derived from posted payslips, never stored. Not a remittance: "remittance" is the cashier's handover of a day's takings (packages/domain/src/remittance/), and no statutory table or file is named with that word. Source type statutory_payment; penalty books to 6810
receipt - Two unrelated meanings across the reference repos. In POS/CUSTOMER/a sale, a receipt is the customer-facing proof of a sale (receiptSeq, receiptId on a sale/kitchen ticket — see the entry above). In ERP-rebuild's AP module, ReceiptPlain (types/index.ts:441) is a supplier invoice — what a supplier bills you, broken into one or more expenses postings over time. v2 never uses "receipt" for the supplier-invoice sense — that table is supplier_invoices (T-130) precisely to avoid this collision. If you mean the sale-side document, say *sales receipt*; if you mean a supplier's bill, say *supplier invoice*. Never bare "receipt" in this codebase

title: Money and books (cont.)
text:
owed (remittance) - What a store's cashier drawer still has to hand over for one date: that date's cashier-cash movement (journal lines on 1110-1130 held by the cashier) minus what posted remittances already allocated to it. Derived on read in repo/remittance.ts, never stored. A date can owe money whether or not anyone has verified its sales day
remittable - Not "this money may be remitted." It is sales_days.status = 'verified' for that date (repo/remittance.ts:99): a statement about the sales day, not about the cash. A day that is not remittable can be holding real cash in the drawer right now, and the remittance screen shows that cash anyway
settleable - A date a handover can be applied to: remittable and owed > 0. createRemittance allocates oldest-first across settleable dates only, and refuses before any write when there are none
variance (remittance) - Signed. Handed over minus what the settleable days owed: negative is short, positive is over, zero is an exact match (remittance/allocate.ts). varianceDayId says where the arithmetic put the difference (the last day that owed anything), never who caused it

title: Money and books (cont.)
text:
float (till) - money_accounts.float_target: the amount a cashier drawer is meant to keep (at most one per store). At a float store a handover carries only what the verified days owe, and the float stays in the drawer; extra float goes back to the office as a transfer
overdraft (money account) - An outflow that would take an account below zero. A property of the account, not the feature (bible rows 154, 161): a cashier drawer is warned and still posts (its sales are not in the books until verify), down to a per-account cap admin sets; an office or staff account is refused

title: Identity
text:
person - One human being, independent of how they authenticate. A staff member who is also a loyalty customer is one person
display_name - A person's name as shown everywhere. Since T-438 (migration 0207) it is DERIVED when last_name / first_name / middle_name are set: Last, First M. (the CHECK persons_name_parts_check enforces it). Legacy rows, terminals and the usage author have NULL parts and keep a free-text display_name; parts are never guessed from it, they are retyped once on the staff page
person_identity - One way a person is recognised: firebase_uid, phone, email, staff_no, device_hash. Many per person. Phone is an identity, never a primary key — it changes. DEF-009

title: Identity (cont.)
text:
Employee ID - T-464. What a staff member types on a PAIRED POS tablet: the NUMBER of the badge code employments.staff_code, 1-3 digits (7, 07, 007 all mean SE-007). It is not person_identities(kind='staff_no') (nothing writes that kind; it is unique globally, not per store). The code is ALWAYS allocated by allocateStaffCode (never typed), always SE- + 3 or more digits (CHECK, migration 0212), and no two codes at one store share a number. It names an employment AT THAT STORE, so a person at two stores has two Employee IDs
paired tablet / pairing - T-464. A store's POS tablet that a manager or admin set up once (pos_tablet_pairings, one live row per store). The browser holds a random secret in the httpOnly cookie shareat_pos_tablet; the server stores only its keyed hash. Revoked on un-pair or replacement; dead after 30 days unused
staff vs diner - A *role*, not a table. Both are persons
platformAdmin - A Firebase custom claim granting cross-store admin. Distinct from staff/{uid}.status === 'active'; either passes CUSTOMER's admin gate

title: Places and structure
text:
org / organization - The legal entity. One row today; SEBN reserved as the second
store / branch - A trading location. store is the schema word — prefer it. Every store-scoped table carries store_id
commissary - A store that produces and dispatches to other branches rather than serving diners. storeKind === 'commissary'
branch sale - Commissary → branch dispatch booked as revenue. System-booked, never typed into a form
channel - Where an order came from — walk-in, Grab, Foodpanda, branch sales. A dimension (channel_id) on journal lines, not a set of accounts
Lane A / mirror - Postgres → Firestore, server-written, client read-only. Staleness is expected and tolerated
Lane B / inbox - Device → Firestore, append-only. Raw facts only, never computed outcomes. The server adjudicates
the four verbs - How anything is carried across from a reference repo: duplicate what's good, correct what's wrong, add what's missing, delete what's redundant
reference repos - ERP-rebuild, POS, CUSTOMER, Shareat Website. All four are READ-ONLY. Nothing is ever fixed at the source — findings go to DEFECTS-REGISTER.md

title: Repo names — the trap
text:
v1, the legacy ERP, the old system - The live production ERP being replaced - webapps\ERP-rebuild
the reference repos - All four read-only sources - ERP-rebuild, POS, CUSTOMER, Shareat Website
this project, Shareat System - The rebuild - webapps\shareat-system
ERP-rebuild is the OLD system. Its name says "rebuild" because it was itself a rebuild of something older. A cold agent reasonably reads that folder name as *this* project and starts editing a live production system. It is read-only, like the other three.

title: Slicer pay (T-635)
text:
performed_by_person_id - who sliced a slice record; NOT created_by (whoever typed it) or posted_by
confirmed_by_person_id / confirmed_at - another staff member checked the slicing; never the slicer; cleared by an edit
is_paid (production line) - an OUTPUT line the slicer is paid per kg for; false = re-cut or trimming
paid_by_pay_run_id (production record) - the posted pay run that paid it; set on post, cleared on void; while set the record cannot be edited or voided
slicer_pay (payslip) - per-kg pay in gross, NOT in basic_pay
worked_as (punch / day / adjustment) - regular or slicer. The punch carries what the person chose at clock-in (null = no choice = regular); the day's value is DERIVED on every recompute (first clock-in, or a live worked_as adjustment); a slicer day pays 0 from the daily rate
isSlicer (roster mirror document) - the offline kiosk asks only these people "Working today as: Slicer / Regular staff"
slicer_days / slicer_earlier_records (payslip) - days paid as slicer days (days_worked is the REGULAR days); records paid that were confirmed late, from before the period

title: Words we deliberately avoid
text:
"v1" for this project - legacy ERP / Shareat System - "v1" means the legacy ERP in ~170 places. This project has no version number
"dine-in" for a metric - name the account — 4100 unli, 4150 à la carte - "dine-in" is ambiguous exactly where it matters
"sync" between apps - publish (Lane A) or ingest (Lane B) - "Sync" implies bidirectional. Nothing here is bidirectional
"the API" - name the app and route - Four apps had eight cross-app routes. Ambiguity here caused real bugs

title: The rules, in one place
text:
This is a digest, not an authority. Every rule cites its section in PROJECT_BIBLE.md, which wins any disagreement — if this file and the bible differ, this file is stale and that is a bug worth fixing. It exists because the bible is long and an agent starting cold needs the operating rules without reading 1,600 lines of architecture first. Read this to start working; read the bible before deciding anything.
---

title: 1. Never — the hard constraints
text:
1 - All four reference repos are READ-ONLY — ERP-rebuild, POS, CUSTOMER, Shareat Website. No edits, no branches, no git. A defect found there is logged and fixed *here*, never patched at the source - §2.1 · row 80
2 - ERP-rebuild is the OLD system despite its name. This project is webapps/shareat-system - §2.1
3 - Never touch webapps/inactive projects — exclude it from every recursive search - §2.2
4 - Postgres is the sole system of record. No entity's authoritative state lives on a device or in Firestore - §2.3
5 - Device-held data is one-way except the outbox. The POS tablet keeps a server-written snapshot and an append-only outbox posted to /api/pos/events; the clock still uses Firestore under the same rule until its move - §2.4 · §5 · rows 280, 430
6 - No money in floats. numeric in the DB, integer centavos in code - §2.5 · §6
7 - No client-side-only authorization. Every gate exists server-side - §2.6 · §7
8 - No implementation without a written task spec in docs/tasks/ - §2.7 · §3

title: 1. Never — the hard constraints (cont.)
text:
9 - Every schema change is a migration. An applied migration is never edited — write a new one. And it is HAND-AUTHORED — npm run db:generate is retired and fails closed; the checklist is ADR-012 §5 (DEF-242; bible §13 row 191; packages/db/migrations/README.md) - §2.8 · §15.5 · ADR-012
10 - Stop the dev server before npm run build — the build clobbers the .next it is serving - §2.9
11 - NEVER BUILD ON EITHER DROPLET — and know which is which (DEF-238). [address] is OUR production host: erp2.shareat.net, the shareat-erp service, /srv/shareat-shared/.env.local. [address] is the OLD SHARED droplet (ERPNext + the POS archive DB) — this project has never run there; /srv is empty on it. Both are small boxes and a build OOMs either. Builds run in CI; the server receives a finished artifact. Until 2026-09-08 this rule named only the old droplet and called it "the production droplet", which sent people to the wrong machine *and* said nothing about the real one - §2.10
12 - Port 9008 is ERPv2's alone; 5435 for local Postgres. Never pass a different -p - §2.11

title: 1. Never — the hard constraints (cont.)
text:
13 - An app may never import from another app. Apps depend on packages/; packages never depend on apps. *Enforced by tests/unit/app-boundaries.test.ts* - §8 · ADR-004
14 - Only the Opus planner amends the bible. An implementer reports a needed amendment and stops. A spec that lists the bible in its Scope is a defect in the spec - §14 · row 86
---

title: 2. How work is done
text:
Research → plan → spec → implement. A new phase, module, or any data shape expensive to undo gets a bounded research pass first, producing a document under docs/discovery/. Research informs; it never decides — the target is the midpoint (§1.1), so the output must name what we are not adopting and why - §3.6 · row 96
Pick the model for the task. Sonnet = the default for delegated work (code reading, discovery, executing a spec, tests). Opus = planning, architecture, specs, review. Fable = *only* a bug that survived a deliberate Opus pass, or genuinely intricate data-shape design. *"It was hard" is not the escalation bar* — and do not spend Opus on what Sonnet does well. Whole lane terminals too (Ian, 2026-09-08): a worker executing an approved spec runs on Sonnet; the orchestrator names the model in the briefing; a session cannot switch itself, so Ian types /model and the board lists which terminals - §3.1a · rows 93, 184
A spec names the exact files you may touch. Stay inside it. If you must go outside, say so explicitly in your report - §3.3
Tests before implementation, and confirm they fail *for the right reason* first. A test that only ever passed proves nothing - §3.2 · §9

title: 2. How work is done (cont.)
text:
Integration tests run against real Postgres, never a mock - §9.3
Smoketest in the running app. A green build and green tests have already shipped an app that could not start - §9.4
Report a spec defect; never silently work around it. A planner's spec is a hypothesis — patching around a defect destroys the evidence it was wrong - §3.4a · row 97
Verify, do not claim. Report the command's real output. *A task reported complete with a failing gate is worse than one reported blocked* - §3.4a · row 97
Every subagent prompt is self-contained — it starts cold and knows nothing of the conversation - §3.4
Parallel agents must share no STATE, not merely no files. Two agents running test:integration against the one shareat_test database truncate each other's fixtures. Before parallelising, ask what else is shared: the test DB, migrations/meta/_journal.json, a port - §3.4 · row 94
Prefer a guard to ! on a regex match, and where ! is used, a comment names what makes it safe. noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on deliberately and ! is the one remedy that silently switches it off at the point of use - §13 row 206

title: 2. How work is done (cont.)
text:
Messages are short (Ian, 2026-09-24). A status line, real numbers, paths, and what the reader must act on. No narration, no restated brief, no bare ACKs. Ian hears only what needs him. Reports 15 lines or fewer, FINDINGS 30 or fewer. Evidence is never cut - §3.5a
Every question for Ian goes on the Open Questions page (Ian, 2026-09-30) — https://claude.ai/artifact/LMQCEXDZqHyAJz69FCy7FN, collection questions via ArtifactData: plain words, an example, options with one recommended, a priority. Read it at session start and before building anything gated on Ian — an answer typed there is his ruling. Answers given in chat are copied there too - §13 row 252
Every report ends with a FOR IAN block — plain language, what changed, what needs a decision - §3.5

title: Definition of done — all of it, every time
text:
typecheck clean · unit tests pass · integration tests pass against real Postgres — and the FULL suite before anything reaches main, not just the lane's files (Ian, 2026-09-22; DEF-412 is what a lane-scoped gate hides). Since 2026-10-08 that full suite runs in CI on a PULL REQUEST, not on the laptop: push a branch, open a PR, merge to main only when its CI is green (bible row 291). Since 2026-10-09 that PR goes up ONCE, at wrap-up, carrying the day's slices (bible row 296) — except a slice Ian needs live early, or one carrying a migration (its own PR, or prechecks with Ian before wrap-up); after every local commit run the guard and census files plus the affected tests. Locally, run only the tests a change can affect · smoketested in the running app on 9008 · npm run build succeeds with the dev server stopped · self-reviewed line by line · committed with a message explaining *why* · bible amended if a decision was made. *Reporting done when any of these is unmet is itself a defect.* — §9

title: 3. How to read the reference repos
text:
v1 owns the GOAL, never the method; a better way is welcome (Ian, 2026-10-06). Every v2 design pass invokes /research-evaluate-propose first. Redesign, screens included, is allowed wherever it is more user-friendly; no v1 capability is silently dropped; a redesigned POS screen goes to Ian as a mock-up first - §13 row 283
Read them as REQUIREMENTS, not as design. Every feature exists because the business needed it and staff use it daily. The code may be wrong; the *need* is proven. Authoritative about WHAT, never about HOW - §1.2b · row 84
UI/UX is a third authority. A screen should be familiar-but-upgraded, never reinvented — same record workflow, better presentation. One uniform, reusable pattern set across screens. apps/erp/pos/customer are one visual family. POS, not ERP-rebuild, is today's presentation-quality benchmark where the two disagree - §1.2c · row 171

title: 3. How to read the reference repos (cont.)
text:
v1 is the flawed version; v2 is the improved one — and discovery has a METHOD, in this order. Study v1 at source → write down the GOAL it was built to achieve (an unwritten goal can only be copied, never improved on) → count the live data: populated, consistent, and actually consumed by anything downstream? → design v2 against that goal, the bar being *more accurate, more correct, more effective, more efficient*, not merely *not-flawed*. Bad data downgrades v1 from proven practice to evidence of the NEED only — then the v2 rule is designed, not ported - §1.2d · row 172
Reading needs no permission and no announcement. Read freely and often — guessing what the old system does is far more dangerous than opening it - §2.1
The four verbs: *duplicate* what's good · *correct* what's wrong · *add* what's missing · *delete* what's redundant - §1.2
If a feature looks pointless, ASK — never delete. Removing a redundant *implementation* is Claude's call; removing a *capability someone uses* is Ian's - §1.2
Where v1 and correct accounting disagree, practice wins — and the divergence is recorded. A v1-vs-v2 accounting difference is a finding, not a failure - §1.3

title: 3. How to read the reference repos (cont.)
text:
LOG WHAT YOU SEE, EVEN WHEN IT IS NOT YOUR TASK. A bug, gap or flaw you notice in passing while reading v1 for some other reason is logged before you move on. *"I wasn't tasked with that area"* is not a reason to skip it — one row costs nothing, and you are the only person who will ever have that context. Verification is not required: state it as reported; a later session confirms it - §13 row 164
Three doors, and the wrong one buries the finding. v1 does it wrong → docs/DEFECTS-REGISTER.md A–D, cite file:line · v1 does it and no phase owns it → docs/CAPABILITY-GAPS.md (a gap is not a defect — that pass is what caught the five ledger modules January needed) · Shareat System itself is wrong → DEFECTS-REGISTER.md section E - §13 row 164
---

title: 4. Ian's standing directive
text:
Ian describes WHAT. Claude decides HOW. A literal reading of an instruction is not automatically the correct execution of it - §0.1
Brainstorm before executing — name the industry-standard pattern first. Boring and standard beats clever and bespoke - §0.2
Side with the project. Where "what Ian asked for" and "what is best" diverge, build the better one and say plainly that you did, and why - §0.3
Push back, including hard — on scope, on sequencing, on a decision that has turned out wrong. Explicit permission, therefore an obligation. Raise it once, properly; then keep working - §0.4
Not licence for: scope creep · silent substitution · skipping destructive-action confirmations · contrarianism - §0.5

title: 4. Ian's standing directive (cont.)
text:
A requested feature is ASSESSED before it is planned, and may be argued against. Weigh expected utilisation against effort and complexity; say the number, not the adjective. Then research — the industry pattern *and* what already exists on GitHub, because a well-solved problem probably has been solved. Then plan. Recommending against is sanctioned, therefore expected: say it once, plainly, then build it anyway if Ian still wants it. Adopting is not free either — licence, self-hosted vs API, vendor vs depend are part of the assessment, not afterthoughts. Invoke /research-evaluate-propose — the skill that carries these three steps, global, available in every repo - §13 row 163

Why is it built this way? - docs/decisions/ (ADRs) and bible §13, 216 logged decisions
What does this word mean? - docs/GLOSSARY.md — *read before naming anything;* several fields mean the opposite of what they look like

How do I actually run and click the app? (the §9.4 gate) - docs/SMOKETEST.md — from nothing to a signed-in screenshot. Read it before reporting §9.4 as impossible; it has been reported impossible three times on premises that were wrong

title: 6. The three that catch people out
text: 1. dineInSales is package-only, takeOutSales is a residual, receiptSeq is not a monotonic key. Read the glossary before trusting any field name. 2. A defect in a reference repo is never an argument against the feature. The implementation is evidence of a real need, not a proposal to drop it. 3. The database enforces the rules, not the service layer. Do not re-implement balance, period, or immutability checks in TypeScript — a second copy is a second source of truth, and the two will drift. This is about CHECK constraints and triggers (balance, period, immutability) — not tenancy. Tenancy is layered on purpose: the repository filters, RLS backstops (bible §7 rule 4 + §15.11). The binding rule for both is §15.11 — *no layer may be the only one for a given risk*. DEF-210 is what it looks like when one is. (There is no "bible §6.3"; a citation to it means this item — bible §15.11.)
