title: Decision 260 (2026-09-30)
text: IAN'S ANSWERS ON THE OPEN QUESTIONS PAGE, 2026-09-30 — T-367 Q1–Q7, T-369 Q1–Q4, T-371, DEF-443, DEF-476, T-315, T-316 (full list: docs/plans/money-defects-2026-09-30.md). Headlines: a supplier rebate reduces the payable; a paid bill cannot be voided until its payment is; a duplicate write-off by the same person is the same write-off; a voided sales day frees its date but only a manager may re-enter it, never staff ( "re-enter" superseded by row 270: a manager re-IMPORTS from the source, never re-types); an empty money box is refused only when the amount is required, never turned into zero; a cancelled order's thread is read-only; amounts leave page addresses before launch; existing staff get store access through a one-time admin-reviewed list; cashiers count before handing over. Why: Answers typed on the page are rulings (row 252)

title: Decision 261 (2026-10-01)
text: THE MANAGER WHO TOOK A HANDOVER MAY CONFIRM ITS OVERAGE AS INCOME. T-366 S3 shipped recognise_income gated on accept_remittance (manager/admin, not staff — row 253's A1 Q3). It does not exclude the person who recorded the handover, unlike write-off's author check. Why: Ian, 2026-10-01, Open Questions page, recommended by the orchestrator: an overage is cash already in hand — confirming it moves nothing out of the business, so a second pair of eyes buys no protection.

title: Decision 262 (2026-10-01)
text: A SCREEN RENDERS A MONEY CONTROL ONLY WHERE THE VIEWER CAN USE IT; A COUNT OF WORK STAYS ORG-WIDE. Write-off/void on the customer page and Charge/Recognise on the remittance page show only where the viewer holds the capability at that record's store (heldCapabilities + a per-store authorize probe — never the gate itself). The uniform "does not exist, or is not yours" refusal stays for hand-crafted requests. A list may follow the page's store picker, but the count of unresolved work it summarises stays org-wide ("N here · K more at other stores") — row 147, a count must be visible. Why: Orchestrator rulings during the T-367 S1 and T-366 S3 reviews (auditor findings): a control that refuses every click is a lie about what the viewer can do, and the uniform sentence then reads as a fault. Row 147 caught the first version of the remittance ruling, which had scoped the count away with the list.

title: Decision 263 (2026-10-01)
text: VOIDING A SUPPLIER PAYMENT FROM A CLOSED MONTH: THE PERSON PICKS THE REVERSAL DATE (pre-filled with today, must be in an open month). T-369 S0 / DEF-550. Why: Ian, 2026-10-01 (chat), recommended by the orchestrator: the reversal must land in an open month; letting the person choose keeps it on the right business day

title: Decision 264 (2026-10-01)
text: 15TH-AND-30TH PAYDAYS ARE SUPPORTED: the second half is paid on the 30th (last day in February) even when the half ends on the 31st; monthly-on-30 follows the same rule; a run paid on the 30th is still posted after the 31st and dated the 31st. T-370 A3 / S3b, DEF-553. Why: Ian, 2026-10-01 (chat + Open Questions): 15/30 is the common Philippine schedule; the old roll-over made staff wait ~a month and paid two periods on one date

title: Decision 265 (2026-10-01)
text: A STORE MAY PAY FROM ANOTHER STORE'S MONEY: the safe that paid goes down (credit at the ACCOUNT's store) and 1250 Due from / 2150 Due to (party = the other store's code) record what the owing store owes. Applies to reimbursements, expense approval and AP payments (T-369 S8, DEF-551) and to AR collections and loan disbursement/repayment, gated on transfer_funds at the account's store (S8b, DEF-556). A collection may land in another store's cashier drawer with no extra drawer rule; opposite inter-store debts are not offset on paper (settled by moving cash). Why: Ian, 2026-10-01 (chat + Open Questions), recommended by the orchestrator: each store's books must show the cash it really holds

title: Decision 266 (2026-10-01)
text: A 'SETTLE BETWEEN STORES' TRANSFER CLEARS WHAT ONE STORE OWES ANOTHER (1250/2150 for the pair; transfer_funds at BOTH stores; partial allowed; capped at the net both books agree on). T-369 S9, DEF-557. Why: Ian, 2026-10-01 (Open Questions) — without it a repaying transfer grows both balances

title: Decision 267 (2026-10-02)
text: COMMISSARY RECEIPT MISMATCHES (T-372 S6, amendment 2): SHORT (sent 10, received 9) → the floating unit is charged to a commissary staff member (charge) or absorbed as an expense for broken/spoiled-in-flight (loss); OVER (sent 10, received 11) → the branch books what was sent, the extra is an 'over' row blocking the commissary's day-open, settled by the commissary manager confirming it really sent more (extra_dispatch posts commissary −1 / branch +1 at layer cost); a branch MISCOUNT is closed as a recount return with a note, initiated only by the manager of the store initiating the return (the branch). Why: Ian, 2026-10-01/02 (Open Questions); refines rows' T-372 Q3 (i)

title: Decision 268 (2026-10-01)
text: THE AUDITOR LANE STAYS SONNET; an external AI is at most an optional second pass, only when Ian asks. A GPT-6 trial on T-369 S4 (docs/reviews/external-audit-t369-s4.md) found 1 real new issue, 2 known-deferred gaps and 1 false positive, and missed the 3 money findings Sonnet caught. Local dev uses the IN-MEMORY storage driver (FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET commented out in .env.local) so tests never write to the private bucket; the one test photo that reached it was deleted. Why: Ian, 2026-10-01 (chat)

title: Decision 269 (2026-10-04)
text: POS v1 AND CUSTOMER v1 ARE COPIED INTO apps/pos AND apps/customer AT A PINNED COMMIT, THEN HARDENED AND SWAPPED ONTO THE ERP v2 BACKEND — ONE POSTGRES, ONE AUTH, THREE APPS — BY ENTITY-OWNER FLIPS, NEVER DUAL-WRITE. Ian, 2026-10-04: *"pos v1, customer v1 will also be reworked since we intend them to share same backend postgres db shared auth for 3 projects. so the shape of erp shall assume this"*; *"copying the pos v1 ... then improve that and modify so it fits the backend of erpv2"*. Phases E (ERP now), P0 copy and harden, P1 reference data and auth, P2 receipts, P3 live tables and CUSTOMER (docs/decisions/ADR-015-pos-and-customer-on-the-shared-backend.md). UI and interaction are copied (§1.2c); rules and data layer stay requirements-only (§1.2b). The reference repos stay read-only (row 80). Ian's POS rulings, 2026-10-04: pos-q0 retired (this plan adopted); qa (a) the copied POS goes live after 1 Jan 2027, one store first; qb (a) POS and CUSTOMER table and order state move to Postgres together, per store, at P3. Supersedes: ADR-003's "never two at once" for the POS + CUSTOMER pair; §1.2b for POS/CUSTOMER UI only; §8's 9003/9004 for apps/pos/apps/customer (those are v1's ports — new ports at P0). Why: Ian's drivers: (a) one source of truth, (c) getting off Firebase. Discovery 22 §1: the screens are the good part and staff are fluent in them; the 139 files of client-Firestore coupling are the work. ADR-003 already set this end state; the copy is how it is delivered. December i

title: Decision 270 (2026-10-04)
text: SALES DATA IS NEVER TYPED OR EDITED IN THE ERP. THE SALES DAY IS A DERIVED CLOSING OVER A SOURCE — THE POS v1 DAY FEED NOW, POS RECEIPTS FROM P2 — AND A DATABASE TRIGGER REFUSES ANY FIGURE WRITE OUTSIDE THE DERIVATION. A WRONG SALE OR DISCOUNT IS REVERSED ON THE POS, AS A REFUND. Ian, 2026-10-04 (Open Questions t371-blank-on-edit): *"all sales data must be from pos that cant be edited if needed reversing discount must be done on POS as refund"*. Other edit screens (late charge, production labour) keep "blank keeps the stored figure". The usage pull, the day feed and shareat-hub-v2 retire per store as receipts arrive (P2). Built by T-375 (docs/tasks/375-pos-v1-day-feed.md); today's typed form is DEF-586. Supersedes: ADR-005's sales bridge mechanism ("POSv2 is far out" — the bridge now retires per store at P2); row 260's "a manager may re-enter" a voided sales day, which becomes a manager re-IMPORT, never a re-type. Why: One source of truth: a figure typed in two places drifts, and a "From POS" checkbox checked against nothing proves nothing (DEF-586). Industry standard (ERPNext POS closing, Odoo): the daily posting is a summary over sales documents, and nobody edits a closed sale

title: Decision 271 (2026-10-04)
text: THE POS v1 DAY FEED'S INTERIM RULES (pos-q1..q4, Ian 2026-10-04): (q1 b) PLATFORM SALES (Foodpanda/Grab) STAY A SEPARATE ERP ENTRY OUTSIDE THE POS-LOCKED FIGURES, FOR NOW; (q2 a) THE FEED'S DISCOUNT TOTAL POSTS AS ONE 4900 LINE; (q3 a) A POS CHANGE AFTER VERIFY BECOMES A FINDING PLUS A CORRECTING ENTRY IN AN OPEN MONTH; (q4 a) NO MANUAL FALLBACK — IF POS IS UNREACHABLE THE DAY WAITS. q1 verbatim: *"a separate platform-sales entry stays in the ERP, outside the POS-locked figures — but i plan to include this to pos soon for now build as B"* (the orchestrator recommended (a); Ian chose (b)). Each rule stops mattering for a store when it reaches P2. Why: v1's feed carries one discountsTotal (POS/src/app/api/external/sales/route.ts:93-94); the split arrives with receipts (row 218). A typed fallback would reopen the hole row 270 closes

title: Decision 272 (2026-10-04)
text: A CLOSED RECEIPT IS IMMUTABLE: THE POS COPY REMOVES EDIT AND VOID OF CLOSED RECEIPTS IN P0; MISTAKES ARE REFUNDED (pos-q5 (a)). Ian, 2026-10-04. A refund is a new receipt with parent_receipt_id, dated the day it happens. Why: We now own the copy, so the fix is in the code, not a staff policy. Industry standard: refunds are reversing documents; nobody edits a closed sale

title: Decision 273 (2026-10-04)
text: ONE LOYALTY PROGRAMME ACROSS ALL ORGS; POINTS ARE A LIABILITY OF THE ISSUING ORG, SETTLED BETWEEN ORGS (Q-C (a)). Ian, 2026-10-04. A diner is a person with a phone identity, never an AR customer and never a Firebase Auth user (DEF-343); a diner principal is needed (persons.org_id is NOT NULL today). Points redeemed post to 4910. Built at P3. Why: A diner earns at Lipa (own books) and redeems at Padre Garcia (franchise, separate books, ADR-008); one programme keeps the diner's experience, the issuing-org liability keeps each set of books honest

title: Decision 274 (2026-10-04)
text: ONE POSTGRES. NO HOT/COLD SPLIT, NO ARCHIVE DATABASE, NO REPLICA NOW. A STANDBY, A READ REPLICA OR PARTITIONING IS ADDED ONLY ON A MEASURED TRIGGER — standby when POS P2 goes live and failover in minutes is wanted; replica when reports pass ~30% CPU; partitioning when one table passes 50M rows. A nightly off-cluster dump with a rehearsed restore is required (§15.8). Firebase is NOT the system of record (§2 rule 3 restated). Ian, 2026-10-04, from docs/discovery/pos-offline-and-data-tiers-proposal.md §2. Why: Estimated POS load is under 1.5M rows and ~1 GB a year; through 2028 about 2–4 GB in total. A second database breaks the ledger's single history and puts a cross-database join in every report

title: Decision 275 (2026-10-04)
text: SUPERSEDED BY ROW 280 (Ian, 2026-10-05). WAS PROVISIONAL — PENDING IAN'S CONFIRMATION. FIREBASE EXIT SCOPE, WORKING DEFAULT (b): OFF FIREBASE AS DATABASE AND AUTH; KEEP ONLY FCM PUSH FOR THE CUSTOMER APP; THE CLOCK TERMINAL MOVES TO THE SAME ON-DEVICE OFFLINE APPROACH AS POS. Ian named "getting off Firebase" as a driver (row 269) but has not picked the scope; this is the orchestrator's working default so planning can proceed. If confirmed: the §5 Lane A/B rules stay, but their carrier becomes the device's own outbox posting to the shared backend instead of Firestore; Firebase Auth stops being a credential kind. Until confirmed, nothing beyond P0 is built on either answer (ADR-015 §6). Would supersede: rows 2, 4, 10, 11, §5.2's Firestore move, and the target of row 202 (all marked provisionally in place). Why: Driver (c); one fewer vendor holding business state; the clock and the till should not run two different offline mechanisms

title: Decision 276 (2026-10-04)
text: POS SELLS OFFLINE FOR 24 HOURS (BASIC ORDERING AND BILLING), PER DEVICE, ON THE TABLET'S OWN STORAGE. WIDENS ROW 77. Ian, 2026-10-04: *"pos needs to be offline resilient like it can be used in basic billing and order taking for 24hrs"*; *"since we are making pos as apk can we use device storage as temp storage in offline setting?"* Rules (ADR-015 §5): offline, a table is billed only on the device that opened it (other devices send refills and kitchen tickets); the outbox and the receipt sequence live in IndexedDB (SQLite if the soak fails), never localStorage; receipt numbers are (store, terminal_no, seq), continuous and never reset (DEF-587); every offline sale prints paper, and an X-reading slip prints every 4 offline hours; the device RECORDS a sale and the server recomputes and compares (§5.4 rule-1 carve-out); offline PIN sign-in against a device-only verifier (P1). Acceptance gate: a 24-hour soak on two real tablets, zero loss, zero duplicates. No LAN hub and no local database per store; the hub is reconsidered at P3 only if two devices must bill one table offline. Supersedes: row 77's 10-minute-to-1-hour tolerance and its pre-allocated-block numbering option; §5.3's closed list for POS (entries added at P1 per ADR-015). Why: Industry standard (Square, Toast): store-and-forward on each device. The real limit is not storage but that two tablets cannot see each other with the internet down; the owner rule handles it without hardware. Per-device continuous numbering matche

title: Decision 277 (2026-10-04)
text: other AND ar_collection ARE RETIRED AS v2 EXPENSE PAYMENT METHODS (T-367 Amendment A1 FINAL, DEF-054, migration 0182). Ian, 2026-10-04 (QA1): *"i dont want others as payment now its ambigious"*. v1's 322 other rows were all system-written (depreciation 297, amortization 23, disposal 2) and 0 were staff vouchers, which v2 already models natively (T-124, T-125). The QA2/QA3 rows (one rebate, one store credit, 2 online-order-expense docs, 3 manual platform fees) are decided by Ian by hand at the cutover audit, with no tool. Supplier vouchers get their own home: a CAPABILITY-GAPS row (Ian: they *"should have a home now"*). Supersedes row 258's split of v1 other into rebate/voucher methods and its suspense landing: nothing lands in suspense. Why: One method, one meaning. The cutover is opening-balance only (rows 83, 105, 109), so no v1 expense document reaches the v2 ledger and an ETL skip rule would protect nothing (docs/tasks/367-ap-ar-money.md A1)

title: Decision 278 (2026-10-04)
text: A PUSH TO main IS A PRODUCTION DEPLOY. ci.yml runs on push; deploy.yml runs on its successful workflow_run and ships to [address]. Therefore every read-only precheck for a migration not yet on production runs BEFORE the push, never after (docs/ops/README.md, Deploy gate). Recorded 2026-10-04 because only the ops README and deploy.yml's header said it; no decision row did. Why: Ian's T-205 decision to auto-deploy every green push. Row 228 (push only at wrap-up) is the cadence; this row is the consequence: the wrap-up push is the deploy

title: Decision 279 (2026-10-05)
text: IAN'S RULINGS ON T-316 AND T-375 (Open Questions page, 2026-10-05). (t316-early-handover a) at a float store a handover may take only what verified days owe; today's cash waits for verification — as built in S2. (t316-overspend-refill transfer) the office tops an overspent float back up by transfer — as built; sales do not refill it. (t375-q1 new key) a new store-scoped POS API key is made on POS's side for v2 and the same value placed on our server; v1's key is not reused (Ian needs the steps; an ops task, blocks linking a store on production, not building). (t375-q2 income) POS "charges" post to other income 4500; no store bills a staff service charge through POS. (t375-q3 a) every POS v1 refund is treated as paid from the cash drawer; the till count shows it if it went back by another method. (t375-q4) Ian: *"we include vat to final price and for now VAT is only a label the vat remittance computation is handled manually and separately. pos only send out bill not invoice"* — no store is VAT-exclusive; no output-VAT liability is posted from the feed (row 75 stands); T-375's VAT-exclusive refusal stays as a guard that should never fire. Why: Answers typed on the Open Questions page (row 252) are Ian's rulings. q1–q3 match the recommended defaults already built or specced; q4 confirms row 75

title: Decision 280 (2026-10-05)
text: FIREBASE EXIT: COMPLETELY OFF FIREBASE — DATABASE, SIGN-IN, AND PUSH. THE CUSTOMER APP SENDS NO PUSH NOTIFICATIONS; THE CLOCK TERMINAL MOVES TO THE SAME ON-DEVICE OFFLINE APPROACH AS POS. SUPERSEDES ROW 275. Ian, 2026-10-05 (firebase-exit-scope), answering the option that kept only FCM push: *"no need for this once ready it will just be served — we do not complicate things here; furthermore most customers are assumed to not pay much attention on app while dining, they just use that when ordering and asking for assistance."* Read as: the one thing (b) kept (an "order ready" push) is not wanted, so nothing in Firebase stays. Hosting and file storage follow the same rule ("do not complicate") and move with the apps; their replacement is planning detail for the phase that moves them. Rows 2, 4, 10, 11, §5.2's Firestore move and row 202's target, marked under row 275, are superseded on this answer when the phase that replaces them is planned; nothing beyond P0 changes today. Why: Driver (c) of row 269; one fewer vendor holding business state; the diner uses the app to order and call for help, not to wait for alerts

title: Decision 281 (2026-10-05)
text: THE POS USAGE PULL (AND THE SALES PULL) ARE TO BE REDESIGNED FOR THE UNIFIED BACKEND, NOT POLISHED. PLAN IT WITH /research-evaluate-propose BEFORE T-375 S5 IS BUILT; UNTIL THEN THE BUILT T-374 VOID RULE (a) STANDS. Ian (t374-q1-pull-void-who, answered on the Open Questions page; found unrecorded and recorded 2026-10-05): *"need to redesign this pull from pos. this sales and inventory/usage pull from pos exist because v1 backend are separate/different now in v2 we have unified backend so this can be improved, changed, replaced with. plan this and suggest using research evaluate propose skill"*. Interim (POS v1 still separate) is T-375's day feed and S5's stored sold_items; the end state (ADR-015, one Postgres) has POS receipts written where the ERP reads them, so no pull exists. The proposal must say which pieces survive into the interim and which are built only to be thrown away. Why: v1 pulled because its backends were separate; v2 will not be (rows 269, 274). A pull redesigned once beats one polished twice

title: Decision 282 (2026-10-05)
text: IAN'S RULINGS ON THE POS PULL REDESIGN (pull-qa..qd, Open Questions page): (Q-A a) AT THE END STATE A DAY'S STOCK USAGE POSTS BY ITSELF RIGHT AFTER VERIFY; A ROOM UNDER COUNT WAITS AND POSTS WITH ONE CLICK AFTER THE COUNT. (Q-B, Ian's own answer) A REFUNDED OR VOIDED RECEIPT'S ITEMS GO INTO A PENDING ("FLOATING") STATE, AND A MANAGER OR ADMIN DECIDES EACH ITEM — BACK TO STOCK OR NOT; NOTHING IS RESTOCKED AUTOMATICALLY. (Q-C a) MANAGERS, ADMINS AND SUPER ADMINS MAY VOID A DAY'S USAGE AND REDO IT, IN BOTH PHASES (AS BUILT). (Q-D a) A DAY TYPED BEFORE ITS STORE WAS LINKED GETS NO POS USAGE PULL; ITS USAGE IS RECORDED BY HAND. Ian, verbatim on Q-B: *"refund and voided receipts will float affected stocks and amanger and admin has to decide on them individually"*. Consequences: T-375 S5 becomes the proposal's S5-lite (stored sold items only, no capture path, typed days refused); the P2 spec carries a pending-restock queue per refunded/voided receipt line with a manager/admin decision and an audit row. Why: Answers typed on the Open Questions page are rulings (row 252). Q-B chooses a decision queue over either blanket rule: food made is usually waste, a sealed item usually is not, and only a person at the store knows which

title: Decision 283 (2026-10-06)
text: v1 OWNS THE GOAL, NEVER THE METHOD — AND v2 MAY REDESIGN, SCREENS INCLUDED, WHEREVER THE RESULT IS MORE USER-FRIENDLY. EVERY v2 DESIGN RUNS /research-evaluate-propose FIRST. Ian, 2026-10-06: *"in designing v2 employ /research-evaluate-propose , build it in premise that when i build v1 i know what the goal is but i dont know how will it be achieved so my ways and techniques in v1 can always be improved corrected provided it will give the user desired result at most efficient and effective way. redesigning is allowed just make it user friendly"*; and: *"meaning if there is better way to do things its welcome"*. Three rules. (1) Every v2 design pass (discovery doc, task spec, phase plan) invokes the research-evaluate-propose skill before planning: the goal written down, the effort weighed against the payoff in numbers, the industry pattern and existing solutions researched (row 163, §1.2d). (2) v1's ways and techniques are never a constraint, only evidence of the goal: the bar is the user's desired result, delivered most efficiently and effectively (strengthens §1.2b and §1.2d step 4). (3) Redesign is allowed, including screens and interaction, judged by user-friendliness for the staff who use it. This LOOSENS §1.2c's *"familiar, not reinvented"* and row 269's *"UI and interaction are copied"* for POS/CUSTOMER: familiarity becomes one input to user-friendliness, not the floor. Unchanged: §1.2d's completeness guarantee (no v1 capability silently dropped; removing one is still Ian

title: Decision 284 (2026-10-07)
text: LIPA IS LINKED TO POS v1 ON MONDAY 12 OCTOBER 2026 (T-375, the first production link). Ian, 2026-10-07: *"link lipa on monday"*, after Lipa's 90-day census returned GATE PASS (T-375 S0: 90/90 days, every refusal count 0; methods Bank Transfer, Cash, Gcash, QRPH; charges on 64 days). Before the link: the push carrying T-379/T-380 S1a lands on production, and Lipa's four POS payment methods are mapped to money accounts on erp2 with Ian. From that business date Lipa's sales days come only from the POS import (0185's lock); earlier days stay typed. Why: A Monday start keeps a sales week from coming from two sources

title: Decision 285 (2026-10-08)
text: A GUARDED POS UNLINK (T-382, migration 0187). R1 soft unlink: three columns on the link row, never a delete. R3 an unlink refuses while the store has an unverified imported day. R4 0187 hardens 0185: no imported figure, tender or remitted row changes on an unlinked store, even under the derivation flag. R5 the import re-reads the whole link (id, updatedAt, POS id) under the store lock after its fetch and refuses on any change. R6 new capability unlink_store_from_pos, super-admin only, backfilled to existing owners (R6a, 0166 pattern). R7 a usage pull on an imported day no longer needs a live link. R8 relink is an UPDATE of the same row. R9 DROPPED (the full UNIQUE on pos_store_id stays, so an unlinked store keeps holding its POS id and no other store can link it). R10 (DEF-607) a POS store id whose sales were ever imported for one store is refused for any other store of the org, live link or not, relinked away or not, because the same sales would be booked twice. R9a a correction or recheck on a day imported under an earlier link refuses after a relink (judged on database-stamped times: feed fetched_at vs link updated_at). "Linked" now means a LIVE link row Why: Delete the link row plus an audit row (needs a DELETE grant 0183 left out and loses who/when/why on the screen); partial UNIQUE on live links (double import)

title: Decision 286 (2026-10-08)
text: A STORE MANAGER IS A ROLE AN ADMIN ASSIGNS, NEVER A SEEDED POSITION; STORE READINESS WARNS (NON-BLOCKING) WHEN A STORE HAS NONE (T-338). Ian, 2026-09-24 (recorded in docs/tasks/338-store-readiness-manager-warning.md; written here at the 2026-10-08 wrap-up): one organisation-wide admin, managers scoped per store, the adminless-manager elevation stays as it is; the readiness checklist gains a manager check that counts only active manager-role holders scoped to the store (admins do not count). Built 2026-10-08. Why: A decision that lived only in a task doc

title: Decision 287 (2026-10-08)
text: AN ITEM'S UNIT STAYS EDITABLE UNTIL THE ITEM HAS ANY RECORD, THEN IS LOCKED; A WRONG UNIT ON A USED ITEM IS FIXED BY RETIRE-AND-RECREATE, NEVER BY RESTATING HISTORY (T-378 Q1 = a). Ian, Open Questions t378-q1-unit-history, answered 2026-10-07: *"If there is no ledger transaction on that item, like newly created, allow edit; if there is then a."* This is the behaviour T-378 already ships (0186: items_base_unit_fixed). Not built: the restate tool (Q1 b). Follow-up: the small rename screen option (a) needs, because item names are unique (items_org_name_key; T-378 N2) Why: A ruling given on the Open Questions page and not yet written here

title: Decision 288 (2026-10-08)
text: EVERY PAGE AND EVERY FORM USES THE FULL WIDTH AND ADAPTS TO THE SCREEN; ONLY SIGN-IN, SETUP AND THE CLOCK KIOSK STAY NARROW CENTRED CARDS (T-384 S2). Ian, 2026-10-08: *"i want all forms to adjust based on screen size and always use full width"*. No form density and no width cap on table; fields sit in a grid that adapts to the space available (FormGrid/Field), never fixed narrow widths. On the three narrow screens (Open Questions t384-q1-narrow-screens): *"add them to narrow card, stack cards horizontally, mid balance always"* — several cards sit side by side, wrapping on small screens, always centred Why: The POS link screen and 12 other pages still sat at 768 px after DEF-440's W2 ruling; Ian said *"again"*

title: Decision 289 (2026-10-08)
text: A SAVED RECORD OPENS LOCKED BEHIND ONE EDIT BUTTON; EDIT UNLOCKS ONLY THAT RECORD AND SHOWS SAVE AND CANCEL; AN ADD FORM ALWAYS ENDS IN SAVE; BUTTONS THAT POST MONEY, MOVE STOCK, CHANGE A STATUS OR GRANT ACCESS KEEP THEIR OWN VERB (T-384 S3). Ian, 2026-10-08: *"save buttons existing must be renamed to edit, lock the fields and only allow edit once edit is clicked then save. implement this globally so user will not be misdirected"*; command buttons: Open Questions t384-q2-command-buttons = a. One record open at a time; Cancel restores the stored values; a save carries the record's version and is refused if the record changed since it was opened. One shared component (EditableRecord) and guard tests (G7/G8) enforce it app-wide Why: Lipa's tender setup (8 Oct): editable-looking rows and a hidden refusal read as "overwritten" and "only 3 allowed"; the audit log showed nothing was overwritten

title: Decision 290 (2026-10-08)
text: RENAME IS SUPER-ADMIN ONLY, ONE NAME FOR THE WHOLE BUSINESS; RETIRING AN ITEM THAT STILL HAS STOCK WARNS AND THEN ALLOWS IT, AND THE ITEM STAYS USABLE FOR CONSUMPTION AND MOVEMENT UNTIL ITS STOCK IS USED UP (T-383). Ian, 2026-10-08, Open Questions t383-q1-who-renames (*"super admin only 1 name for entire business"*) and t383-q2-retire-with-stock (*"yes warning then allow until fully utilized"*). A retired item can no longer be ordered, received or given a new price or POS map; POS usage, recipes, wastage, transfers and counts still work on it until on-hand is zero Why: Row 287's retire-and-recreate needs the old name freed; stock already on hand must still be consumable

title: Decision 291 (2026-10-08)
text: THE FULL SUITE BEFORE main RUNS IN CI ON A PULL REQUEST, NOT ON THE LAPTOP. Ian, 2026-10-08: *"use the PR route from now on"*. To ship: push a branch, open a PR (ci.yml runs typecheck, unit, integration and build on pull_request), merge to main only when that CI is green; the merge's own CI then gates the deploy. Locally, lanes and the orchestrator run only the tests a change can affect (the lane's files, the guards it touches, vitest --changed), plus the §9.4 browser smoke. Migration prechecks (row 278) still run against production BEFORE the merge Why: Local full gates took 40 min to 5.6 h (laptop sleep, load from parallel lanes) and twice reported load timeouts as failures; CI runs the same suite in ~17 min on clean machines. The full suite still guards main (DEF-412)

title: Decision 292 (2026-10-09)
text: POS'S "COLLECTED" METHOD IS A CASH SALE: MAP IT TO A SECOND CASH TENDER (NO MONEY ACCOUNT), AND RECORD WHERE THE CASH WENT THE SAME DAY — AN OWNER DRAWING OR PART OF THE DAY'S REMITTANCE. Ian, 2026-10-09: *"collected is cash remitted earlier or collected by owner"*; Open Questions pos-collected-lipa = a. POS counts it once, inside total sales, never also under Cash (POS external/sales/route.ts). A wallet tender cannot point at a cash account, and a dummy account would hold nothing and double-count with the drawing. Still open on the page: does the owner usually keep it, and who at Lipa records it Why: Lipa's POS lists "collected" (₱0 for 90 days to 6 Oct); an unmapped method refuses the whole import

title: Decision 293 (2026-10-09)
text: A SALES DAY IS VERIFIED AND POSTED ONLY AFTER IT IS SUBMITTED, AND THE PERSON WHO SUBMITTED IT MAY NOT VERIFY IT — EXCEPT A SUPER-ADMIN (T-385, migration 0188). Ian, 2026-10-09: *"verify and post must be blocked until submitted"*; Open Questions t385-q1-different-verifier = a. The domain refuses, a database trigger refuses any change into verified that is not from submitted with a submitter, and the new super-admin-only capability verify_own_sales_day is the one exception. The day page shows Verify & post only where it can succeed and tells the submitter why not Why: Before this, a draft day could be posted directly and one person could submit and verify their own day (the capability matrix said they should not; nothing enforced it)

title: Decision 294 (2026-10-09)
text: ITEM CODES ARE SUGGESTED FROM THE NAME IN ONE FIXED 8-CHARACTER SHAPE, CHWN-001 (4 LETTERS BY A FIXED RULE + A 3-DIGIT NUMBER PER STEM, NEVER REUSED); ONLY A SUPER-ADMIN MAY OVERRIDE, TO THE SAME SHAPE; EXISTING ITEMS ARE RE-CODED ONCE; A RENAME KEEPS THE CODE BUT OFFERS THE NEW SUGGESTION (T-386, migration 0189). Ian, 2026-10-09: *"item code must be auto suggest based on the typed name fixed length with our own way how to formulate the code this way we can control duplication of code to avoid it"*; Open Questions item-code-q1-format = b, q2-override = a, q3-existing = a, q4-rename = a. Codes become unique ignoring case; the number is assigned at creation from a forward-only counter Why: v1 has no item code; v2 codes were free-typed, case-sensitive, and could collide between pending requests

title: Decision 295 (2026-10-09)
text: THE ERP LOOKS LIKE THE BRAND: "SHAREAT WARM" IN LIGHT (CREAM GROUND, WARM INK, BALOO 2 HEADINGS, PLUS JAKARTA SANS BODY, 12PX ROUNDED-RECTANGLE BUTTONS, PILLS ONLY FOR BADGES AND CHIPS) AND "GRILL NIGHT" IN DARK (WARM CHARCOAL). ADR-013 AMENDMENT 7. Ian, 2026-10-09: *"go with B, C as dark mode"*, chosen from a rendered brand and app sheet (Artifact L7hn691wjL76rSV2BgPa1A). Every earlier ADR-013 rule stands: one red primary, outlined danger, warning never as text, one control size, ring-ink. New tokens --field-border, --brand-ink, --warning-ink, --muted and status softs. This closes the dark --brand-as-text and dark --warning gaps (Amendment 4). C's 52px floor density and its gold focus ring are NOT adopted Why: v2 had tokens but no brand presence (no logo, font or ground) and no status, toast or field-error language. The Website already declares this palette and these fonts, and v1 staff know Baloo 2 and pills

title: Decision 296 (2026-10-09)
text: GITHUB CI RUNS ONCE A DAY, AT WRAP-UP: THE DAY'S SLICES ARE COMMITTED LOCALLY AND GO UP TOGETHER IN ONE PULL REQUEST; MERGE (AND SO DEPLOY) ONLY WHEN ITS CI IS GREEN AND WITH IAN'S GO. AMENDS ROW 291 (WHICH STILL SAYS WHERE THE FULL SUITE RUNS); TWO EXCEPTIONS. Ian, 2026-10-09: *"new rule only work github ci on wrap up"*, then *"yes, record it with both exceptions"*. Exception 1 — unblock Ian: a slice that must be live before Ian can act (e.g. T-386 S5: the production recode dry run needs the script deployed) may go up in its own early PR, only with Ian's go. Exception 2 — migrations: a slice carrying a migration goes in its own PR, or at the least has its prechecks (row 278) run with Ian before wrap-up, so one bad precheck cannot hold back the whole day's batch. The local backstop: because CI no longer runs per slice, after every local commit the orchestrator runs the guard and census files plus the affected tests (not only the lane's files) — merged lanes breaking each other's guards is the failure this rule would otherwise hide until wrap-up Why: One CI run takes 20-25 min; per-slice PRs spent hours waiting on CI and on merges. Fits the standing push-once-at-wrap-up practice. Cost: a red batch is harder to attribute (bisect the day's commits), and production changes only once a day — both covered by the backstop and the two exceptions

title: Decision 297 (2026-10-10)
text: A POS USAGE PULL SECTION IS "FINALIZED" ONLY WHEN EVERY CONFIRMED LINE HAS POSTED. A LINE THAT CANNOT POST — ITS ITEM SHORT IN ITS ROOM OR IN THE STORE'S LAYERS, ITS ROOM UNDER COUNT, OR ITS ROOM UNABLE TO TAKE USAGE — IS HELD BACK AND NAMED IN WORDS; EVERY OTHER LINE POSTS; FINALIZING AGAIN POSTS THE HELD LINES ONCE. STOCK NEVER GOES BELOW ZERO, SO A SALE CANNOT BE FORCED OUT OF STOCK THAT IS NOT THERE (T-388; SUPERSEDES T-177 INVARIANTS 4 AND 9). Ian, 2026-10-10, Open Questions def-618-pull-short-stock = a, and t388-q1-old-dropped-lines = a (sections finalized before the fix stay as they are) Why: Before T-388 one short item skipped its whole room's usage, the section was stamped anyway, and the screen blamed a "frozen location" (DEF-618); a closed month stamped with nothing posted (DEF-620); a room short but stocked elsewhere failed with raw trigger text (DEF-619)

title: Decision 298 (2026-10-10)
text: WORK FASTER: SEVEN PRACTICES ARE STANDING. (1) one worktree per lane, so 2-3 tasks run at once; (2) shared fixture builders for the heavy setups (an item with stock AND its layer, a POS sales day with a pull, a closed month); (3) lane databases created from a pre-migrated template; (4) unit tests run with fewer threads / a longer timeout so heavy guards stop timing out; (5) the Workflow tool for sweep-shaped work (the same change over many files, e.g. T-389 S2-S4), one agent per file, with the same tester-first red and the same audit; (6) specs written ahead, several at once, each money/auth spec reviewed by a fresh Opus; (7) the auditor reviews while the builder works. Ian, 2026-10-10: *"approved all including 5"* Why: Measured 10 Oct: one worktree serialised every task; testers spent 3-16 min per slice on setup and 3 of 4 slices bounced on fixture defects; every full unit run showed 4-15 false timeouts; spec → review → fixes ran one after another

title: Decision 299 (2026-10-10)
text: PIN SIGN-IN HAS A DAILY BUDGET: EVERY ATTEMPT IS CHARGED AS A MISS BEFORE THE PIN IS CHECKED, AND A SUCCESS REFUNDS ONLY ITS OWN CHARGE; 50 MISSES IN THE ROLLING 24 HOURS STOP PIN SIGN-IN AT THAT STORE; A CORRECT PIN DOES NOT RESET THE BUDGET; THE ATTEMPT LOG FEEDS TWO SOFT FINDINGS; A STOPPED STORE STAYS STOPPED UNTIL ANYONE HOLDING enrol_staff AT THAT STORE REOPENS IT (T-395 R2-R5, R12, R14). Spec docs/tasks/395-pin-sign-in-throttle.md §Rulings. Two rulings at build (orchestrator, 2026-10-10): *"the last 7 Manila days"* means today and the 6 days before; a stopped store's figure counts the 24 hours before the stop, not before now. Tier 1 (10 / 60 s / 2 min) is unchanged. Findings are soft, never hard, so a sign-in problem never blocks a period close. Commits 9264324 (S1, migration 0190), 3954f31 (S2) Why: Tier 1 alone allowed about 13,000 guesses a day per store (about 32 % to hit a 6-digit PIN); 50 a day is about 0.15 %. Checking before charging let parallel attempts race past the count (DEF-626). A budget that refills on its own is a slower tier 1: a human looking is the point

title: Decision 300 (2026-10-10)
text: A REFUSED SAVE KEEPS WHAT WAS TYPED THROUGH ONE TYPED SLOT IN THE FLASH (SIGNED, ONE MINUTE, BOUND TO THE PERSON, THE RECORD AND THE FORM). FOR RECORD FORMS IT SUPERSEDES T-380'S PER-FIELD keep. THE SERVER DRAWS ONLY STORED VALUES, SO CANCEL RESTORES THEM; THE TYPING COMES BACK THROUGH THE TYPED VIEW (T-389 R1-R5). Spec docs/tasks/389-refused-save-keeps-typing.md. T-380's mutant M4 was re-pointed to the typed slot. Field names may contain a hyphen (/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/) so per-channel rows are kept. Business identifiers may be kept (organisation TIN, store branch code); personal statutory ids, PINs, credentials and bank account numbers never are (the deny list, R4, guard G10). Only fields named in changed ride the cookie. Commits 1da8e60 (S2), a4d533f (S3) Why: Losing a whole form to one refused field is the defect. A per-field keep had to be wired form by form and mixed typed and stored values in one view, so Cancel could not tell them apart. One slot, one helper, one guard covers every record form

title: Decision 301 (2026-10-10)
text: AN OPENING COUNT BELONGS TO A ROOM, AND EVERY COUNT ROW CARRIES THE SOURCE OF ITS COST; THERE IS ONE COST PER ITEM PER STORE (T-390 S1, R1-R3, migration 0191). Spec docs/tasks/390-opening-stock-and-subledger-tieout.md. Orchestrator ruling at build, 2026-10-10: a count without a cost never changes any cost, and a new or null-cost room row takes the store's existing cost and its source. Writers serialise per (store, item) with a transaction advisory lock taken after the shared org lock. Commit f75201e Why: Stock is counted room by room, and an opening layer is one per movement. Without a recorded source a cost cannot be audited at cutover. The audit found two concurrent writers left two different costs for one item in one store; the lock closes that

title: Decision 302 (2026-10-10)
text: V2 RUNS EVERYTHING BUILT FROM 1 JANUARY 2027, ATTENDANCE AND PAYROLL INCLUDED; T-190 AND T-193 ARE THE PRIMARY PAYROLL PATH AND T-397 (THE MONTHLY BRIDGE ENTRY) IS THE FALLBACK ONLY. IF THE HR SHEET IS NOT COMPLETE ON 31 OCTOBER, PAYROLL STAYS ON V1 AND STAFF WITHOUT STATUTORY IDS ARE HIRED WITHOUT THEM. PHASE 7 AND THE THEME WORK FOLLOW CUTOVER WITH V1 KEPT LIVE FOR THEM; THE REVOLVING FUND (T-136 §2) FOLLOWS CUTOVER; T-315 IS CLOSED AS MOOT. Ian, Open Questions page, 2026-10-10: plan-q1 = (a), plan-q10 = (a), plan-q11 = (a), plan-q9 = (a), plan-q13 = (a). Plan docs/plans/remaining-build-plan.md §0b, §1.1 C9, §3.2 Why: Ian chose (a) over the recommended (b) for q1: one cutover, not a second one on 1 Mar. The 31 Oct HR sheet is therefore the hinge: on time, T-190/T-193 are specced and built in waves 2-4; late, q10 (a) applies and T-397 is built instead. Production has no pre-fix staff, so T-315's backfill has nothing to fix. Standing floats (T-366) cover store cash on 1 Jan

title: Decision 303 (2026-10-10)
text: THE DUAL RUN "TIES" WHEN CASH AND BANK, SALES BY TENDER, EXPENSES BY CATEGORY AND AP PER SUPPLIER AGREE TO THE CENTAVO PER STORE-WEEK; INVENTORY AND COGS ARE SHOWN AS ONE NAMED POLICY DIFFERENCE, NEVER AS A FAILURE. LIPA DOUBLE-ENTERS FROM 19 OCTOBER, ALL FOUR STORES FROM 2 NOVEMBER, ONE OFFICE ENCODER PER STORE. CASHIERS AND OTHER POSITIONS WITH STAFF ROLES ENCODE; THE MANAGER VERIFIES. EACH LINKED STORE'S CLOSED DAY IS FETCHED BY A TIMER AT 06:00 MANILA; SUBMIT AND VERIFY STAY HUMAN. Ian, 2026-10-10: plan-q2 = (b), plan-q3 = (b), plan-q6 = (a), plan-q12 (free text): *"cashiers and other positions with staff roles encode; the manager verifies"*. Binds T-392 (comparator) and T-396 (timer) Why: v1 expenses stock on purchase; v2 is perpetual FIFO, so a whole-trial-balance tie is impossible by design. Lipa first finds the friction before four stores do. The encoder/verifier split is row 293's separation of duties in operational terms

title: Decision 304 (2026-10-10)
text: OPENING STOCK IS COUNTED PER ROOM AT THE COMMISSARY AND IN ONE ROOM AT EACH BRANCH, AND IS VALUED AT THE LAST V1 DELIVERY PRICE; AN ITEM V1 NEVER DELIVERED IS PRICED BY A MANAGER TYPING IT. THIS SUPERSEDES §16.11's "THE 2027-01-01 OPENING LAYER IS WEIGHTED AVERAGE" (AND ADR-009's opening-layer row). Ian, 2026-10-10: plan-q8 (free text): *"mirror v1, storage is important for commissary only; for branches and others 1 room only"*; t390-q2 = (a) last v1 delivery price; t390-q1 (Q-T390-1) = (b) the manager types every unpriced item. T-390 S2 is unblocked. Built as data, no code change: T-390 R1 (a branch count with no room goes to the store's default room), R2 (--basis last, cost_source = 'v1_last_delivery'; a typed cost is 'typed') Why: v1 keeps a per-room ledger and storage matters only at the commissary. The last delivery price is the closest to a FIFO layer cost that exists, and it is auditable per row; a weighted average over v1 data that holds no inventory value had no defensible input. The basis still changes exactly once, at the boundary

title: Decision 305 (2026-10-10)
text: THE PADRE GARCIA FRANCHISE RUNS ON V2 BY 1 JANUARY 2027, AS ITS OWN ORGANISATION. ROW 246'S TRIGGER ("before a second organisation is onboarded") THEREFORE FIRES BEFORE CUTOVER: DEF-491 AND DEF-421 BECOME CUTOVER SCOPE. PLAN ITEM C11, TASK T-398 (RESERVED). Ian, 2026-10-10: plan-q4 = (b), against the recommended (a). Plan §1.1 C11 Why: ADR-008 §4-§7 and rows 111, 114, 175 already design the second org (own books, franchisor sees SALES only, commissary dispatch to a franchise is a sale). What is missing is the onboarding itself and the guards a second org needs. scripts/import-items.ts reads every v1 store, Padre Garcia included, into one org: under this row Padre Garcia's items belong to its own org (T-391 must split them)

title: Decision 306 (2026-10-10)
text: BACKUPS: T-393 IS BUILT AND TESTED BUT NOT SWITCHED ON UNTIL IAN SETS IT UP ("no backup for now, we'll set up soon", Ian 2026-10-10, answering every T-393 question). OPEN POINT, NOT RESOLVED HERE: plan-q7 = (a) (the existing shareat-erp-backups bucket under postgres/, prefix-scoped 30-day retention, never touching the Frappe objects) conflicts with the T-393 spec as reviewed (a dedicated shareat-pg-backups bucket, 35 days + 13 monthly + yearly, R5/R12). Ian picks one when he sets it up. Ian, 2026-10-10: plan-q7 = (a); T-393 Q1-Q5 answered "no backup for now" Why: Until it is switched on, production has only DO's native 7-day backups and no restore has ever been rehearsed. The 13 Nov rehearsal (T-394) needs a restored copy and wizard step C1 attests a drill: the 15 Nov go/no-go cannot pass without it (R4)

title: Decision 307 (2026-10-11)
text: POS V2 AND CUSTOMER V2 HAVE NO ADMIN PANELS OF THEIR OWN. MASTER DATA (MENU/CATALOG WITH VARIANTS, FLAVORS, REFILLS, PACKAGES, OPTION GROUPS AND PER-STORE PRICE; STORES; STAFF AND USERS; DISCOUNTS, CHARGES AND TENDERS; LOYALTY REWARDS; STORE SETTINGS — SCHEDULES, TABLES, KITCHEN ROUTING, FORECAST, CUSTOMER ORDERING), DINER CONTENT (FLASH ADS, GAMES MODERATION, FEEDBACK) AND REPORTS ARE EDITED IN ERP V2 ONLY. FLOOR OPERATIONS STAY ON THE APP: TABLE PINS, THE ONLINE-ORDER QUEUE, RECEIPT REPRINT AND REFUND, AND MARKING AN ITEM SOLD OUT (AVAILABILITY) ON THE POS. DEVICE SETTINGS (THERMAL PRINTERS, OFFLINE DEVICE IDENTITY) STAY ON THE DEVICE. CUSTOMER'S SEPARATE categories MASTER IS FOLDED INTO THE ONE ERP MENU. V1's REPAIR SCREENS (reconcile, backfill, rebuild caches) ARE NOT CARRIED. Ian, 2026-10-11, brainstorm session: accepted the three-way split, sold-out on the POS, and categories folded into the menu. Narrows row 269: the POS/CUSTOMER UI copy excludes their admin areas Why: v1 keeps stores, staff, payment methods and menu groupings in two or three apps, synced one way or by hand (POS admin/*, manager/* ≈26 pages; CUSTOMER admin/*, manager/* ≈13 pages; ERP-rebuild inventory/pos-mappings). ADR-003/004 (one product master, one store table) and ADR-015 §2 / row 130 (the till only reads menu, prices, tenders, discounts) already imply one editor; this row names it. Floor actions stay on the till because seconds matter mid-service (row 270 already puts corrections there); printers

title: Decision 308 (2026-10-11)
text: WARM NEUTRALS (T-387). Ian: *"go on and fix the clash in colors."* Tailwind's neutral ramp is re-valued warm in apps/erp/warm-neutral.ts: steps 200/400/500/800/900/950 ARE the ruled Amendment 7 tokens; the other steps keep stock lightness in the ink hue. Side effect, intended: the stock caption grey (4.34:1 on cream, an AA failure) now passes. Why: Ian's ruling; the stock ramp clashed with the warm tokens and failed AA

title: Decision 309 (2026-10-11)
text: DARK --warning-soft = #2b2210 (T-387). Ian: *"keep #2b2210."* ADR-013 A7 had no dark warning-soft; this is it, pinned in theme-tokens.test.ts. Why: Ian's ruling; the token was missing

title: Decision 310 (2026-10-11)
text: ACTIVE NAV IS RED (T-387). Ian: *"make active nav red."* The current nav item fills with --brand, white text, in both themes. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 311 (2026-10-11)
text: ONE RED PRIMARY PER VIEW (T-387). Ian: *"demote extras."* A view has one red primary action; a repeated Save is secondary. SubmitButton gained a variant prop. Ian also ruled *"merge when green"* for every T-387 PR. Why: Ian's ruling; several red buttons on one view diluted the primary action

title: Decision 312 (2026-10-11)
text: TWO T-387 SPEC NOTES. (1) useFormStatus exists in the App Router (Next's bundled React 19) but not in the react-dom 18.3.1 Vitest loads, so tests use the shim apps/erp/tests/helpers/form-status-setup.ts — a test-only bridge, never imported by source. (2) attendance_days RLS is org-level; the store boundary is the repo filter (§15.11 layering), not RLS. Why: Recorded so the next reader does not "fix" the shim or add store RLS

title: Decision 313 (2026-10-13)
text: ONE TABLET PER STORE RUNS THE POS; THE ERP RUNS ON ANY OTHER DEVICE. Ian: *"we only allow 1 tablet per store now"*. There is no second billing tablet, so no in-store server and no tablet-to-tablet sync. Why: Ian's ruling (posv2 plan)

title: Decision 314 (2026-10-13)
text: DINER SIGN-UP PROVES THE PHONE WITH ONE SMS CODE; LOGIN IS PHONE + PASSWORD; ONLY A MANAGER RESETS A PASSWORD, IN PERSON. This followed a read-only count of about 20-25 logins and 15-27 new accounts a month, so codes at sign-up cost under ₱30 a month. There is no self-service reset. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 315 (2026-10-13)
text: RECIPES ARE SHAREAT STANDARDS. Sauce/batch production recipes and the menu guide recipes are edited by admins only and can never be granted below admin. Stores and the Padre Garcia franchise only suggest changes. Slab-slicing yields have no standard and always record actuals. The guide recipe sets expected usage; usage within ±10% (an org default, with an admin override per item) is accepted, and outside it is flagged for the manager's explicit check and a reason before posting. Why: Ian's rulings (T-401, T-403)

title: Decision 316 (2026-10-13)
text: MENU MASTER (T-401) RULINGS. Managers set prices for their own store. Only super admin adds items; managers request them. The online price can be a rule over the counter price (%, ±₱ or fixed). The v1 usage pull switches per store to the menu recipes, after a 7-day comparison, and can switch back. Flavours are an option group. Why: Ian's answers Q1-Q6

title: Decision 317 (2026-10-13)
text: ACTIVITY LOG BUILT NOW (T-402), PULLED FORWARD FROM PHASE 7 A2 (overrides Q11 (a) for this item). It extends the immutable audit_log with a tag and a sensitivity from one fixed catalogue, plus redaction. Retention is 10 years for money/order/menu-price/customer events and 2 years for low-sensitivity events only. Dropping a 2-year partition is a deliberate, catalogued deletion under §4.2 rule 9. Managers see their own store. In an org with no admin, the manager serves as admin for the restricted log. Why: Ian ("build now", "go with recommendation", the admin-less flip)

title: Decision 318 (2026-10-13)
text: POS v2: STORE ORDERS SHOW ON THE POS SCREEN. Commissary orders, transfers and other orders addressed to a store appear on the POS, the always-on screen, so the cashier is notified immediately. Stock-usage drafts are queued from many staff at once, visible to all store staff, and posted by the manager. Why: Ian's rulings

title: Decision 319 (2026-10-14)
text: THE TILL STAYS IN THE ERP; THE POS v2 SCREEN MIRRORS IT. Ian (Q1 of docs/feedback/2026-10-14-ian-feedback-review.md): *"a"*. Till custody (open shift, count, close, charge a shortage, remittance; T-186, T-153, T-143, T-366) stays an ERP record. The POS v2 screen shows and drives the *same* till/shift rows by calling the ERP domain functions on the one Postgres (ADR-015 §4). The POS never owns a second till. Confirms row 130 (POS transacts, ERP accounts). Narrows ADR-015 §2: the POS gains a till *screen*, not a till *entity*; ADR-015 needs an amendment saying so before the POS till task is specified. Why: A POS-owned handover cannot see cashier-paid expenses, cash requests or AP paid from the drawer, so it would force a second entry (review item 1)

title: Decision 320 (2026-10-14)
text: SETTLEMENT FILES ARE PARSED, NOT RETYPED: A GRAB OR FOODPANDA PAYOUT FILE IN ZIP, XLS/XLSX OR PDF BECOMES A DRAFT SETTLEMENT THAT A PERSON POSTS THROUGH THE EXISTING ACTION. NOTHING IS WRITTEN TO v1. Ian (Q2): *"a - it must accept zip xls and pdf files that it will parse and post"*. The parser only fills the input of recordChannelSettlement (same capability, same idempotency, same patterns channel_settlement.plain / .promo_credit); it has no posting path of its own. The store is chosen explicitly on upload, never routed from the filename (v1's "lip 15.zip" → Lipa, discovery 23; row 283). A file or line that does not parse is quarantined with its reason and never half-posted (§5 rule 5); the uploaded file is kept as the settlement's evidence. "Mirrored to v1" means the read-only dual-run comparison (T-392 S1b), so rows 78 and 106 stand. Narrows T-150 ("manual entry first; the parsers are their own task"): that task is now ordered, and manual entry stays as the fallback. Platform *sales* are untouched (row 130): this is the payout, not the sale. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 321 (2026-10-14)
text: A CASHIER SEES EVERY PAYMENT METHOD; THE ACCOUNT'S BALANCE, NOT THE ROLE, DECIDES. ALREADY ENFORCED, SO NO CHANGE. Ian (Q3): *"the cashier must see all payment method with filter based on balance if already enforced then let it be"*. Verified in code 2026-10-14: the expense form's account list is filtered by store, never by role (apps/erp/src/lib/money-lines/load.ts). Each account carries its derived balance, and apps/erp/src/components/money/MoneyLines.tsx shows inline the same judgeDraw verdict the server enforces at approve (packages/domain/src/expenses/approve.ts → checkDraw, summed per account across a split). An office or staff account that cannot cover the draw is refused; a cashier drawer is warned (row 154). The check runs at approve, not at draft (a draft is not a posting). Credit is offered-but-disabled for a COD supplier (T-362). An account short of money is shown with its verdict, not hidden; that verdict is the "filter". Confirms row 154; closes review item 4a. Why: Ian's ruling + code check

title: Decision 322 (2026-10-14)
text: ONE PERSON, ONE ID, BEHIND BOTH THE APP SIGN-IN AND THE CLOCK. THE CLOCK STAYS FINGERPRINT/CARD ONLY, NO PIN; THE PIN SIGNS INTO THE APP. Ian (Q4): *"1 account. coz now v1 has 2 accounts the accountid in local user is different from the log in id, i want them to be just 1 account but still no pin for log in in clock but pin can be used in signing in to use the app"*. Verified in schema 2026-10-14: v2 already has a single id. persons.id is the spine (§7.1). App credentials (person_credentials: pin, firebase, biometric) carry person_id. Clock credentials (attendance_credentials: card, fingerprint) carry employment_id → employments.person_id. Punches carry both person_id and employment_id. A Firebase uid is a person_identities row of that same person, not a second account. The master-data load makes one person per human (T-391 S4, v1_master_links entity person) and imports no v1 credential, so v1's local-user id and its sign-in id never arrive as two people; staff enrol a PIN and a card/fingerprint fresh. No second id was found. The duty now is to keep it so: no feature may add a second identity table. Two credential *tables* stay (a terminal mirror must never carry a PIN verifier, migration 0085); there is one *identity*. Confirms row 165 and §7.1; answers review item 5a with the additive reading. Why: Ian's ruling + schema check

title: Decision 323 (2026-10-14)
text: A STAFF MEMBER WITH TWO OR MORE POSITIONS PICKS THE ONE THEY ARE WORKING AS, AND THE PICK CAN ONLY NARROW. Ian (Q5): *"a"*. After the PIN, and only for a person holding ≥2 positions at that store, sign-in asks which one they are working as. The session records it (acting_position_id, null = all). Position-sourced grants from the *other* positions are dropped inside actor resolution, so the pick can only remove access, never add it. Hand grants and elevations are kept under a pick. Switching mid-shift is a "switch position" action that re-asks for the PIN. The manager/admin *role* is not a position, so a pick never narrows it. actor_person_id stays the person; the acting position is written into the audit row. Supersedes part of row 198 ("a position never enters the check path"): it now enters as a filter on position-sourced grants. What stands of row 198: a position is still never a parameter to authorize(), grants are still materialised, and the ~568 call sites do not change. Plan 289 §4's "Cashier+Cook keeps the union" now holds only for a session with no pick. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 324 (2026-10-14)
text: SOME EXPENSE CATEGORIES NEED NO RECEIPT AT ALL: A TRUE, PER-CATEGORY EXEMPTION. Ian (Q6): *"a"*. A category carries a flag "no receipt needed", and an expense in it posts with no evidence. Reverses T-196 decision 2 ("evidence stays unconditional; needReceipts is not ported"). How exempt spend stays visible and controlled, binding on the spec: (1) only an admin sets the flag, under its own capability, and every change is an audit_log event (T-402 tag), never a silent edit; (2) the flag is stamped onto each expense when it is created, so turning it on later never exempts old spend and turning it off never strands it; (3) a "spend without a receipt" register per store × month (amount, category, who, approver) sits on the manager and admin dashboards; this is the orphan detector T-196's out-of-scope note said an exemption needs; (4) approval, overdraft (rows 154, 321) and the manual doubtful flag (T-363, row 251) apply unchanged; (5) the category list marks the exempt ones plainly. v1 exempted only "Employee Expenses / Incentive", so the seeded default is that one category and every other exemption is an admin act. Whether an exempt expense still needs its supplier-invoice record (T-196) or none at all is a spec question. Why: Ian's ruling. v1's orphan expenses came from the flag with no detector, so the detector ships with the flag

title: Decision 325 (2026-10-14)
text: AN EXPENSE NAMES A DEFINED EXPENSE ITEM, AND THE ITEM FIXES THE CATEGORY. NO FREE TEXT: A NEW ITEM IS REQUESTED, AND A MANAGER APPROVES IT. Ian (Q7): *"yes"*. A separate expense_items master for non-stock spend: name, its category (fixed), default unit, optional default supplier, receipt policy (ties to row 324), active flag. The expense line picks an item and the category is derived, never re-chosen. An unknown item goes to a "request a new expense item" queue (the item-request pattern). A guard refuses an expense item whose name matches a stock item, so stock purchases still go invoice → inventory (T-149). Does not bring back sub_category (dropped by T-229, migration 0134); it replaces it with something that cannot drift. Why: v1's free-text second level produced 8 catch-all categories; T-145 measured the same disease in items (842 records, 385 names)

title: Decision 326 (2026-10-14)
text: CONVERT STAYS THE UNPAID SAME-SLAB RE-CUT; SLICING GAINS PAID/UNPAID, WHO SLICED, AND THE PIECE RATE. Ian (Q8): *"a"*. T-176 §4 stands ("the re-cut constraint is the whole point; do not relax it"). A slice record carries performed_by_person_id, paid/unpaid and a piece rate; a paid slice is what slicer pay reads (hasLiveSlicerPaymentCovering, a stub today). This pulls the recording half of slicer pay forward from Phase 5 (CAPABILITY-GAPS); paying it stays in payroll. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 327 (2026-10-14)
text: A RECURRING TEMPLATE CARRIES ITS TIMING AND BUILDS UP ONE OBLIGATION PER PERIOD FROM THE PERIOD CHOSEN. "LIABILITIES" IS ONE VIEW OF EVERYTHING UNPAID. Ian (Q9): *"when template is created add the recurring timing then build up based on the selected period. liabilities are mixture of recurring expense unpaid, invoices unpaid etc."*. (1) A template already carries its timing (recurring_expenses.interval, anchor_day, next_due_date; T-216). New: on creation the person picks the starting period, and the T-140 runner builds one draft per elapsed period from there, catch-up included. Each is still a draft that never auto-pays (row 183 stands). (2) "Liabilities" becomes a read-only, unified view of what is owed: unpaid recurring drafts, unpaid supplier invoices (AP), open liabilities register balances, unpaid payroll and open loans. Each figure is derived from its own source; none is copied. T-128 §5 stands (no second scheduler; T-140 owns scheduling), and DEF-074 is answered by one view over the sources, not a fourth stored balance (§4.2 rule 7). Which further unpaid kinds join the view is a spec list, not a new decision. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 328 (2026-10-14)
text: A CUSTOMER PRICE LIST STORES THE RULE; EACH ORDER LINE FREEZES THE RATE. Ian (Q10): *"a"*. The list keeps a rate mode (fixed, ±% or ±₱ over a named basis: item cost or the branch price, mirroring item_pricing.pricing_mode). The unit is always the item's base unit (the free-text price_list_items.unit goes). An order line copies the computed rate when it is made, so a later rule change never re-prices history (discovery 19 §3.4). Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 329 (2026-10-14)
text: DESTRUCTIVE BUTTONS HAVE TWO TIERS: RETYPE THE NAME TO RETIRE OR DEACTIVATE; AN ADMIN PIN, CHECKED ON THE SERVER, TO VOID A POSTING, DELETE, RUN A CUTOVER OR SEPARATE A PERSON. Ian (Q11): *"a"*. The server action re-verifies the PIN (T-302's verifier, attempts counted in pin_attempts); a client dialog alone is never the gate (§2 rule 7). Which of the ~45 danger buttons falls in which tier is the spec's census. In an org with no administrator, the row-196 adminless fallback decides whose PIN counts. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 330 (2026-10-14)
text: OCR FIRST, AND LOCAL FIRST: A LIGHTWEIGHT OCR ENGINE RUNNING ON OUR OWN SERVER MAY READ RECEIPTS. OCR PROPOSES, A PERSON DISPOSES. Ian (Q12): *"i lean on ocr first can, if we can employ local lightweight engine to make ocr engine more reliable we do that. local first consideration"*. Narrows row 251: row 251 barred sending receipt photos to an outside AI provider, and that still holds; an engine we host ourselves is allowed. A proposal fills fields and never posts (T-146's rule). Research before build (§3.6): which engine, its accuracy on real Shareat receipts, and its memory. The production host has 4 GB and must never be starved (DEF-238), so the engine may need its own machine or an off-hours queue. The seam (an after-upload event plus a document_proposals table, review item 17) can be built first. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 331 (2026-10-14)
text: THE ERP CUSTOMER SCREEN ALSO SHOWS A DINER'S LOYALTY PROFILE. Ian (Q13): *"yes"*. This needs a new link between an AR customer and a diner person (ADR-008 §11 keeps them apart; row 273: a diner is a person with a phone identity). The link is optional, made by a person, and audited; points stay a liability of the issuing org (row 273). Built at ADR-015 P3 with loyalty. Q14 (the "wastage pull") needs no row: nothing exists to retire. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 332 (2026-10-14)
text: DUAL RUN: THE V2 ENCODER ALSO ENTERS GRAB/FOODPANDA PAYOUTS. During the T-392 dual run the v2 encoder records channel payouts (and so their fees), so channel bank, fee and receivable lines are expected to tie with v1. A missing payout is a real delta, not a policy class. Why: Ian's ruling (2026-10-13 evening / 14), recorded in docs/tasks/392-dual-run-comparator.md "## Ian rulings, 2026-10-13"

title: Decision 333 (2026-10-14)
text: DUAL RUN: A DISPOSITION COUNTS ONLY AFTER A FRESH EXTRACT AND COMPARE. The snapshot is still deleted after every --apply (R3 unchanged). The pack shows "re-run compare" and is not signable until that re-run exists. Ian's laptop must be on for the 15 Nov sign-off run (it does the extract). Why: Ian's ruling (option a), recorded in docs/tasks/392-dual-run-comparator.md "## Ian rulings, 2026-10-13"

title: Decision 334 (2026-10-14)
text: DUAL RUN: ONLY ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN MAY RECORD A DISPOSITION. Checked in the domain, not only the UI: run_cutover AND view_financial_reports at the line's store AND an actor whose role is admin or super_admin. Managers keep run_cutover (T-134 attestations untouched) and see the pages read-only. No new capability. Why: Ian's ruling (option b), recorded in docs/tasks/392-dual-run-comparator.md "## Ian rulings, 2026-10-13"

title: Decision 335 (2026-10-14)
text: STOCK USAGE: MANAGER-POSTED STAFF DRAFTS MOVE STOCK; THE POS USAGE PULL BECOMES A CHECK ONLY. Actual usage is what staff record and the manager posts. The POS pull compares expected (sold x rule) against posted actual and flags a gap beyond ±10%; once T-401 S6 lands it no longer takes stock out. Narrows and extends row 318 (drafts queued by many staff, posted by the manager). Specced as T-401 S6, not yet built. Why: Ian's ruling 2026-10-14, recorded in docs/tasks/401-erp-menu-catalog-master.md (S5 rulings + the Ian ruling line after them)

title: Decision 336 (2026-10-14)
text: HAIKU WHEREVER HAIKU CAN DO THE JOB. Subagents for discovery, greps, count bumps and mechanical sweeps pass model: "haiku"; Sonnet for money, auth and schema lanes; Opus for specs and rulings. Extends rows 184 and 298. Why: Ian, 2026-10-14 (orchestrator session); see also memory note "Discovery on Haiku/Sonnet"

title: Decision 337 (2026-10-15)
text: THE GITHUB REPO STAYS PUBLIC. Answers the open question from 13 Oct. Consequence: nothing secret is ever committed (the secrets/ scan at wrap-up and the no-key-in-repo rules stand), and CI runs on the self-hosted runner as today. Why: Ian, 2026-10-15 (chat); recorded here at the 16 Oct wrap-up

title: Decision 338 (2026-10-15)
text: POS v2 AND CUSTOMER v2 LIVE IN THIS REPO as apps/pos and apps/customer, each with its own tsconfig.json; one Capacitor APK per app, built in CI only, new Android app id for v2, release keystore held as a GitHub secret Ian adds.
