Why: Ian, 2026-10-15; recorded in docs/decisions/ADR-015-pos-and-customer-on-the-shared-backend.md "Amendment 2026-10-15" §A1 and docs/plans/pos-customer-v2-phase-plan.md §3

title: Decision 339 (2026-10-15)
text: T-400 (parallel integration tests) MERGED; TURBOREPO ASSESSED AND DECLINED FOR NOW. PR #18 merged after #26 on a fresh green CI (1516ad7). Turborepo was assessed with numbers during POS/Customer planning: path-filtered per-app CI jobs instead; revisit when per-app build + typecheck exceeds 5 min or a 4th app arrives. Scion is not usable here and is not considered. Why: Ian's plan, 2026-10-15; assessment in docs/plans/pos-customer-v2-phase-plan.md §4 ("Turborepo assessment", "Decision: no Turborepo now")

title: Decision 340 (2026-10-15)
text: ENDED EMPLOYMENT ENDS ACCESS (T-407 Q1-Q3, recommended options). Q1: an owner-manager with an org-wide role and no employment row ever (a franchise owner) may sign in. Q2: access stops when an end date is RECORDED, even a future one. Q3: persons.is_active stays unused and is dropped in a later migration batch. Fixes DEF-649/650. Why: Ian answered Q1-Q3 2026-10-15; recorded in docs/tasks/407-def649-ended-employment-signin.md; merged PR #27, live since the 2e9d72d deploy

title: Decision 341 (2026-10-15)
text: STOCK USAGE, REVISED: THE v1 PULL CREATES PRE-FILLED USAGE DRAFTS; UNPOSTED PULL DRAFTS AUTO-POST AT 14:00 MANILA NEXT DAY. One draft per store+day (+location) at the expected quantity; staff correct lines; the manager posts. A pull draft still unposted at 14:00 the next day auto-posts (out-of-band unexplained lines post at expected), flagged auto_posted, audit stock.usage_auto_posted, by the shareat-usage-auto-post timer. Manual drafts never auto-post. T-388 pull holds retired. All stores at once. Supersedes row 335's "pull becomes a check only". Why: Ian, 2026-10-15 (revised the same day); recorded in docs/tasks/401-erp-menu-catalog-master.md "S6 audit rulings" A1-A12; built T-401 S6, migration 0198, merged a879264

title: Decision 342 (2026-10-15)
text: USAGE CONTROLS AROUND THE AUTO-POST. Day close shows a WARNING for unposted usage and never blocks a sales day. Month close is BLOCKED while pull drafts are unposted, unexplained out-of-band lines remain, or manual usage drafts are open (usage records only; wastage keeps today's rule). A manager scorecard shows auto-posted vs manager-posted per store. Why: Ian, 2026-10-15; docs/tasks/401-erp-menu-catalog-master.md S6 rulings (A6 et al.); built in T-401 S6

title: Decision 343 (2026-10-15)
text: POS/CUSTOMER v2 ROUND-2 ANSWERS. Pay-from-phone is not in v2's first release. Customer notices are on-page only (no push). Feedback links to table + receipt, alerts the manager on 1-2 stars, and invites 4-5 star diners to leave a Google review (link only). Privacy: consent tick at sign-up; members inactive 3 years are deleted. Package = one price per head. Wrong tender: the cashier marks it, a manager-PIN correction entry before shift close; after close, refund + re-ring. Read-only usage counts on v1 data approved (customer + POS). Still open: business-day cut-off, first-store date, v1 freeze, v1 safe-void fix, VAT strictness, recipe questions, admin PIN for email-only admins. Why: Ian, 2026-10-15, on the decisions page (round 2); recorded in docs/decisions/ADR-015-pos-and-customer-on-the-shared-backend.md amendment and docs/plans/pos-customer-v2-phase-plan.md §3

title: Decision 344 (2026-10-15)
text: ACTIVITY-LOG FREE TEXT IS CAPPED AT 500 CODE POINTS plus …[truncated] in the log's after payload; the cap counts code points so an emoji is never split. Source tables keep the full text. Why: Orchestrator ruling 2026-10-15 during the T-402 S3 audit; recorded in docs/tasks/402-activity-log.md S3; merged PR #27

title: Decision 345 (2026-10-15)
text: KEEP AGENTS BUSY (standing). Never leave lanes idle: while CI or tests run, start work that shares no state with them (no edits to files, databases or branches the running gate depends on). Extends row 298 (work-faster practices); row 336 picks the model. Why: Ian, 2026-10-15 (orchestrator session); memory note "Keep agents busy"

title: Decision 346 (2026-10-16)
text: T-408, T-409, T-411, T-412, T-413 SHIPPED ON THE RECOMMENDED ANSWERS, NOT IAN'S. Their questions sit on the decisions page unanswered; the recommended options were built so the lanes could merge. An answer that differs from the recommendation reopens that task as a follow-up. The decisions page lists newest and unanswered questions first. Why: Ian, 2026-10-15 evening ("merge all lanes when built"); each task's Status line says "answered by default only"

title: Decision 347 (2026-10-16)
text: R-AUTO: RELEASING A CASH REQUEST CREATES THE STORE'S STAFF CASH ACCOUNT IF MISSING (Ian, 16 Oct). Open cash requests also appear in the expense payment list ("Name · cash request — Balance") with no staff-account gate; the store is chosen first; approve re-checks each request's live balance under a row lock. Shipped as T-414 (PR #30). Spec: docs/tasks/414-expense-cash-request-source.md. Follow-ups: DEF-657/658/659 Why: Ian, 2026-10-16 (orchestrator session)

title: Decision 348 (2026-10-16)
text: DECISIONS PAGE, ROUND 2 CLOSED (Ian, 16 Oct). Business day ends at the store closing time; after-midnight sales belong to the day that opened. First store on v2: 11 Jan. POS v1 feature freeze from 9 Nov (fixes allowed). Live POS v1 = APK build #238, commit e26d0c1. Yes, connect POS v1 to its safe void now (DEF-651). VAT on supplier invoices: typed from the paper; the VAT list is seen by managers for their own stores and admins for all. Recipes: same cap for ingredients; edit refused while unposted cooks use it; retire refused until menu items are re-mapped. Slicing a blocked item: blocked. Admins without a PIN: the Staff page issues one. Receipt photos: under 1,000 a month; OCR = test locally on 30 receipts first. Two answers DIFFER from what shipped and reopen work: (1) deleting an unposted DRAFT needs NO admin PIN; only posted records do (reopens T-412); (2) recipe-cook ingredients ALSO appear on the daily usage screen, labelled as coming from the recipe (reopens T-409/T-401 usage). Still open: whether diners share the people list with staff (Ian: discuss further). Why: Ian, 2026-10-16, on the decisions page https://claude.ai/artifact/H8YVDBG9nuBDBQi2Sguwrs (answers read by the orchestrator)

title: Decision 349 (2026-10-16)
text: CUSTOMER v2 TAKES OVER customer.shareat.net ONCE STABLE. Customer v2 launches at order.shareat.net (POS v2 at pos2.shareat.net; Android ids net.shareat.order / net.shareat.pos2). When order.shareat.net is working well and stable, customer.shareat.net is pointed at it, and Customer v1 is either retired fully or moved to legacycustomer.shareat.net. Which of the two, and the date, are decided at that time. Why: Ian, 2026-10-16 (orchestrator session)

title: Decision 350 (2026-10-16)
text: DINERS LIVE IN THE SAME PEOPLE LIST AS STAFF, MARKED AS DINERS. When Customer v2 moves to the shared backend, diner accounts are rows in the one people list (one sign-in path, one privacy rule: consent tick, delete after 3 years inactive). A staff member who is also a diner is ONE person. Hard rule: a diner-only person can reach no ERP or POS screen or action; every capability check must prove it with a test that the diner is refused. v1 member data (points, visits) is migrated when Customer v2 is built. Closes the last open question of row 348. Why: Ian, 2026-10-16 (orchestrator session; decisions page said "discuss further")

title: Decision 351 (2026-10-16)
text: POS v2 MONEY ACTIONS GO THROUGH OUR OWN SMALL POS v2 SERVER; MANAGERS APPROVE WITH THEIR ERP v2 PIN. Refunds, tender corrections and unpaid-session voids are done by a POS v2 server in this monorepo (pos2.shareat.net, on [address] as shareat-pos.service, port 9009, memory-capped), never directly from the tablet. A manager approves with the same per-person PIN as ERP v2, verified by the shared PIN code (packages/auth, with the T-416 per-person miss cap); nobody can skip the check from the tablet. The Firestore wire format v1 shares stays unchanged (v2 adds fields beside the old ones). Refunds stay cash-only until the ERP day feed (T-375) reads refundTender. Specs: T-423 (client money core), T-424 (server). Why: Ian, 2026-10-16, in the POS v2 session (plan tingly-questing-pretzel.md); recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 352 (2026-10-16)
text: BUSINESS (B2B) CUSTOMERS USE CUSTOMERS + TRADE ORDERS + AR, NOT A SALES CHANNEL. Shareat has two customer kinds: walk-in/online diners (B2C: dine-in, take-out, online à la carte, bulk orders, through sales channels and the POS) and business customers (B2B, e.g. a samgyup house buying meat, paying cash or on account). B2B sales are a trade order to a named customer (T-132): dispatch bills Dr 1210 per customer / Cr 4300 and relieves stock; payment is an AR collection (T-131/T-226). A sales channel stays a B2C source label only. Gaps to build as T-433: pay-now at dispatch, a printable delivery receipt/invoice, a credit-limit warning with manager override. Why: Ian, 2026-10-16 (orchestrator session, research-evaluate-propose: "plan items 123")

title: Decision 353 (2026-10-16)
text: STAFF AND CUSTOMER PERSONAL INFORMATION IS STRICTLY GUARDED (standing). Personal data of staff and customers (names with contact details, addresses, government IDs, birthdays, photos, PIN data, bank/e-wallet details, B2B customer contacts and balances) is shown only to people whose capability needs it, enforced in the LOADER/domain (never only the UI), store-scoped, and never in exports or logs beyond what the task requires. Signatures are the strictest class: stored only through the file broker (never a data URL), viewable only by payroll staff and admins, never shown in lists, cards or exports, served by a short-lived link, and EVERY view and change is audited. Every new screen or report touching personal data needs a test proving an unauthorised viewer sees nothing. Senior and PWD card numbers and names are enforced at insert in the POS device log (T-572, DEF-823): pos_events.payload keeps the fixed marker [redacted]; only statutory_discount_records holds the real values. Why: Ian, 2026-10-16 (orchestrator session)

title: Decision 354 (2026-10-16)
text: EARLY-PHASE CLOSE-OUT RULINGS. (1) Backups (T-393, Phase 0): switch ON now with one proven restore drill, before the 15 Nov go/no-go (reverses row 306's "no backup for now"). (2) Leave/absence tracking (monthly and yearly caps, Phase 4, never built): BUILD before the 1 Jan go-live. (3) Expanded withholding tax on supplier payments (BIR 1601-E): Shareat does NOT withhold; closed as not applicable. (4) Payroll statutory deductions (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, withholding; T-190, then remittance T-193): start NOW from the official 2026 tables; staff data from the HR sheet when it arrives (due 31 Oct). Why: Ian, 2026-10-16 (orchestrator session, roadmap review)

title: Decision 355 (2026-10-16)
text: LEAVE AND PAYROLL-DEDUCTION RULINGS. Leave (T-436): caps and the 5 legal paid days reset every 1 January; unused legal days are paid out as cash at year end; whole days only at go-live; managers may attach medical-certificate photos (guarded per row 353); pro-rated paid days in the year a person reaches one year of service; nobody approves their own leave (a manager's or admin's own leave needs the super-admin). Payroll (T-190): a government contribution (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) is NOT deducted for a person until that agency's number is on file; the payroll preview lists who is missing what. Backups (T-393): files are not encrypted; the bucket stays private with a bucket-only key. Why: Ian, 2026-10-16 (orchestrator session); the orchestrator noted the penalty risk of skipping contributions

title: Decision 356 (2026-10-17)
text: POS v2 OFFLINE RULES (narrows ADR-015 A3). (1) NO refunds while offline: the tablet says "Refunds need the internet." The server-side manager PIN check (row 351) cannot run offline before P1's offline verifier. (2) Voiding an UNPAID table while offline is allowed only for a signed-in manager or admin; the void is marked voidedOffline, listed by pos2-audit, and reviewed after sync. Spec: T-425 (PC-5). Why: Ian, 2026-10-17, in the POS v2 session; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 357 (2026-10-17)
text: POS v2: NO FIXED TABLES — STAND NUMBERS. A party's "table number" is a numbered stainless stand handed over at seating, not a place on a floor. The POS v2 table screen is a list of OPEN ORDERS BY STAND NUMBER, not a floor map (mock-up v3, PC-7). ~~Open: whether a stand number already in use is refused, and how many stands each store has.~~ Answered by row 371 (v1's fixed stand set, one use at a time, picked by click). Why: Ian, 2026-10-17, comments on the PC-7 mock-ups; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 358 (2026-10-17)
text: POS v2: THE FIRST ORDER MAY HOLD A PACKAGE AND À LA CARTE TOGETHER. v1 forces "start the package, then add items"; v2 lets the first order carry both. Payment screen mock-up: agreed. Why: Ian, 2026-10-17, PC-7 mock-up comments; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 359 (2026-10-17)
text: POS v2: KEEP "CONVERT" AS ITS OWN FEATURE (corrects ADR-015 A4.2). v1's PaymentConvertModal is a GCash cash-in/cash-out service (333 conversions in the live data), not a wrong-tender fix. Ian: keep it, as a separate feature. The wrong-tender correction stays its own document. T-422 dropped Convert with /dashboard: a regression, restored by T-427 (server route like T-424; net-zero move between payment methods as v1 did; no PIN for cashiers as in v1). Why: Ian, 2026-10-17, PC-7 mock-up comments; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 360 (2026-10-17)
text: A PERSON'S NAME IS LAST, FIRST, MIDDLE; OTHER SCREENS SHOW "LAST, FIRST M."; HIRE CREATES THE PERSON FROM THE TYPED NAME. The Hire screen takes Last name, First name and Middle name as three fields; every other screen shows Lastname, Firstname M. (middle name reduced to its initial). The "Create new person named" radio is dropped: a name typed into Who-is-this creates the person on save (searching still never creates one). Task T-438. Why: Ian, 2026-10-17, on the Hire screen while hiring Lipa's manager; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 361 (2026-10-17)
text: SIGN-IN BY ROLE: MANAGER, ADMIN AND SUPER-ADMIN MAY USE BOTH PIN AND EMAIL/PASSWORD; A STAFF-ROLE PERSON SIGNS IN ONLY WITH THE TERMINAL PIN. Today manager/admin/super_admin already may use both; the change is that email/password is refused for a person whose only role is staff, even if an email account is linked. Task T-438. Why: Ian, 2026-10-17, asking which sign-in a manager uses; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 362 (2026-10-17)
text: THE BUILT-IN POSITION "COOK" IS RENAMED "KITCHEN STAFF". The canonical six become Cashier, Kitchen Staff, Server, Dishwasher, Slicer, Inventory Staff. Existing canonical rows are renamed in place (same position id, same grants), by migration 0208; new orgs are seeded with the new name. Same day: the six canonical positions were backfilled on production (T-335 script) and Lipa's hand-made Cashier/DishWasher/Server were retired by Ian. Task T-439. Why: Ian, 2026-10-17, after the production positions backfill; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 363 (2026-10-17)
text: LIVE FIELD CHECKS ON EVERY FORM FIELD THAT HAS A RULE. Where a field has a requirement (required, length, allowed characters, a pattern, a range), the form shows a helper line saying what is still missing as the user types, turns it green ("good", "valid") once satisfied, and keeps Save disabled until every rule on the form passes. Fields with no rule are untouched. The server still validates every save (row 7 / §2.6: no client-only rules); the live check mirrors the server rule from ONE shared definition so the two cannot drift. Task T-440 maps every form. Why: Ian, 2026-10-17; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 364 (2026-10-17)
text: ONE PHOTO-UPLOAD CONTROL EVERYWHERE: SHOW STATE, PROGRESS AND A PREVIEW. Every photo upload uses one control: empty = a rounded square (or a circle for a person's photo) on a gray background with an upload icon; uploading = a filling-water style progress animation; done = the preview inside the shape; clicking the preview opens the full-size picture. Guarded files (signatures, leave certificates, staff photos; rows 353, T-434, T-436) keep their own read rules: the full-size view uses the same short-lived audited link, never a public URL. Task T-441 maps every upload. Why: Ian, 2026-10-17; recorded by the orchestrator

title: Decision 365 (2026-10-17)
text: PAYING THE AGENCIES (T-193): ONE EMPLOYER NUMBER, PENALTY BOOKED WHEN PAID, ACCOUNT 6810, NO VOID OF A PAID MONTH. (1) One employer number per agency for the whole company, not per branch (q-t193-employer-no a). (2) Late-payment penalties: the report shows an ESTIMATE only; the real penalty is booked when it is paid, from the agency's receipt. Nothing is accrued automatically. This amends §16.5 requirement 4 (penalty accrual) (q-t193-penalty a). (3) Penalties go to a NEW account 6810 Penalties and surcharges, not 6900 (q-t193-penalty-account a). (4) A payroll run whose month was already paid to an agency cannot be voided until that agency payment is voided first; the books never show an agency as overpaid by accident (q-t193-void-paid-month a). title: Decision 389 (2026-10-26)
text: A BILL THE SYSTEM MAKES WHEN PADRE GARCIA RECEIVES A LIPA SHIPMENT NEEDS NO SECOND CHECKER (T-398 S5d, QI-2 = A). When PG counts in a Lipa (commissary) shipment, the receive step creates PG's supplier bill to Lipa and marks it system-made. A system-made bill is exempt from the two-person verification rule (0046/0217) only while its total equals the shipment's received total and it is linked to that shipment; only the receive path can set the mark, the app role can neither set nor clear it, and its amount cannot be edited. Every other supplier bill keeps the two-person rule. Lipa is the commissary; Malvar is a Lipa branch supplied by stock transfer inside the same org; PG buys from Lipa as a franchise (Ian, 26 Oct). Why: Ian, in chat: "a". Nobody types the amount (counted quantity x Lipa's rate), the 06:30 reconciliation compares both books daily, and the receiver is usually a PG manager, so a second checker would add a daily manual step and delay what PG owes. A made-up system verifier (B) was rejected: it puts a person who does not exist in the audit trail.

title: Decision 390 (2026-10-23)
text: POS v2 DAY CLOSE: THE BUSINESS DAY RUNS Z TO Z; SELLING CONTINUES AFTER A Z; THE CASHIER OR MANAGER CLOSES, A MANAGER APPROVES WITH THEIR ERP PIN. Implements row 348 (the day ends at the store's closing time) as the moment the manager closes the day with a Z-reading, so no per-store closing-time setting is needed; the first Z starts 04:00 Manila of the store's first day; a forgotten Z makes the next one span two dates. A Z does not lock the till: later sales are the next business day. X-readings need no PIN. Both slips say "cash control, not a BIR document" (the POS is not BIR-accredited; official receipts are handwritten, knowledge/staff/cashier-dine-in-sop.md). The ERP's sales day keeps v1's midnight feed until P2. Spec: T-471. Why: Ian, 2026-10-23, POS v2 session (three questions, all as recommended)

title: Decision 392 (2026-10-24)
text: THE NIGHTLY RECEIPT BRIDGE (T-472): ITS OWN READ-ONLY KEY, NO PERSONAL DATA, AND IT CATCHES LATE CHANGES. (1) It reads POS Firestore directly with a new production service account holding only Cloud Datastore Viewer on shareat-hub-v2 (pos-receipt-bridge-readonly), never the POS v2 server key (that one can write). (2) It copies NO personal details: no senior/PWD names or ID numbers, no customer name/TIN/address; statutory_discount_records and the Firestore logbook export stay the source. Supersedes Ian's earlier same-day answer to the POS v2 session (a separate locked table), given before he knew that table existed and that T-435 gates screens, not tables. (3) Edits, voids and late offline syncs older than 7 days are caught with change-time queries. Business day key stays the calendar day with the Z number as an attribute (row 390). Why: Ian, 2026-10-24, via the orchestrator ("1 yes, 2 A, 4 yes")

title: Decision 393 (2026-10-24)
text: A REFUND NUMBER IS CALLED "UNUSED" ONLY AFTER THE SERVER HAS CLOSED IT; A LATE RECEIPT REACHES THE NEXT Z HOWEVER LATE; A Z NEVER ENDS BEFORE THE LAST ONE (T-474, CORRECTS T-470 RULING 4 AND T-471 CORRECTION 3). (1) Refunds (DEF-756): a missing receiptNumbers/{number} is not a final outcome, because the refund request can still commit later and a skipped ledger row is never looked at again. After the 10-minute wait the tablet asks the server (POST /api/pos2/refund-numbers/release) to close the number in one transaction (released: true); the refund transaction already refuses a used number, so a closed number can never carry money. Only a closed number is marked skipped; a number the server answers "used" is acknowledged; anything else stays reserved for a person. Industry pattern: a fence (tombstone). (2) Late receipts (DEF-758): T-471 Correction 3's 7-day lookback is withdrawn. A Z reads in-window receipts by sale time AND every receipt that arrived on the server since the last Z's clock; "counted once" uses every Z committed since that clock. Ruling 5 holds with no time limit. (3) Z boundary (DEF-757): inside the Z transaction, if the latest Z ends at or after this request's clock, the Z is refused 409 and nothing is written. (4) Slip (DEF-759): manual cash adjustments are returned and printed, so the slip's cash lines add up to expected cash (completes T-471 Fix B). Why: Codex read-only audits of 23 Oct (findings 5-8), re-verified on claude/pos-v2-t470 51b5b4f; Opus planne

title: Decision 399 (2026-10-26)
text: A MONTH CANNOT CLOSE WHILE A SALES DAY DATED IN IT IS UNPOSTED; A SALES DAY CAN BE VERIFIED INTO A CLOSED MONTH ONLY THROUGH THE ADMIN CLOSED-MONTH OVERRIDE (T-487, DEF-779). Reverses the ADR-006 §8.2 note that left sales days out of the close gate. (1) closePeriod's draft gate now also counts sales days dated in the period with status open or submitted, POS-sourced or typed; verified and voided never block. The old note said open can mean "today is still happening" — true for today, never for a month that has ended, and a day left unposted there is revenue the ledger never receives. (2) verifySalesDay refuses a closed month in words (the approveExpense sentence pair) and takes the existing admin-only override_period_lock override, which writes a period_overrides row; a locked month never takes it. (3) Reopening stays never built (ADR-006). Why: Audit finding F15 (Claude accounting-core pass, 26 Oct), re-verified on main 26605d1; Opus planner (AUDIT session) under Ian's 2026-10-26 instruction to fix the money findings

title: Decision 400 (2026-10-27)
text: A STOCK QUANTITY ROUNDS HALF-UP, AWAY FROM ZERO, AT THE THIRD DECIMAL, ONCE, AT THE END (T-489, DEF-780). Quantities are numeric(14,3); a conversion factor is numeric(14,6). quantity × factor is computed exactly in scaled integers (multiplyQuantityByFactor, packages/core/src/money.ts), never through a float, and rounded once to three decimals, half-up away from zero — the same rule money already follows (multiply, multiplyToMoney). A received quantity above zero that converts to zero base units is REFUSED, never skipped as "nothing arrived". Records a rule the code already implied but no document named (§6 says only "never float"). Why: Audit finding F20 (Claude posting-paths pass, 26 Oct): toBaseUnits applied the factor at three decimals through a float and truncated, so 0.0625 became 0.063 and a factor under 0.0005 received nothing. Opus planner (AUDIT session)

title: Decision 401 (2026-10-27)
text: A FORM'S REQUEST ID IS ONE TRANSACTION: A REPLAY MUST MATCH BOTH ITS LINES AND ITS ENTRY DATE, OR IT IS REFUSED (T-488 S2, DEF-787; CORRECTS T-488 RULING 3, WHICH COMPARED LINES ONLY). Since T-488 the nine owner, liability, loan and supplier-refund postings key on a per-form requestId instead of (document, date, amount) (bible §4.2 rule 10). postEntry answers a known key before it reads the date, so a lost response followed by the same form re-sent with a CHANGED date returned the original entry as success. postEntryOnce now compares the saved header's entry_date too, as dates only (never re-resolving the period, so an unchanged retry still succeeds after its month closed); a mismatch is refused with "This was already recorded with different figures. Reload the page and try again." Nothing in the ledger is moved or rewritten. Why: Codex audit 17th pass (request-id-replay-ignores-entry-date, F24), confirmed on main 822e7ec; Opus planner (AUDIT session); task number ruled by the orchestrator

title: Decision 402 (2026-10-28)
text: A CUSTOMER CASH REFUND IS PAID FROM A MONEY ACCOUNT OF THE STORE THAT MAKES THE REFUND; ANOTHER STORE'S ACCOUNT, OR A STAFF CASH FLOAT (1120), IS REFUSED (T-493 S2, DEF-797). recordCustomerReturn (external sale, cash refund) now refuses, before any stock moves, a money account whose store is not the order's store ("That money account belongs to another store. A refund is paid from this store's own cash.") and a 1120 staff float (a float belongs to one person's cash request, as payroll and service charges already rule). No inter-store refund path is built: stores do not pay each other's refunds. Customer collections and AP payments already guard cross-store money with transfer_funds and inter-store legs; refunds simply do not cross stores. Why: Audit finding F23 (Claude posting-paths pass, 26 Oct); Ian's ruling, 2026-10-28, in the AUDIT session: "yes refuse" (offered: refuse vs allow with a transfer)

Why: Ian, 2026-10-30 ("why are you setting up these data yourself... create the ui so admin user can set rates"); PR #104

title: Decision 407 (2026-10-31)
text: CREATING A FRANCHISE COMPANY STAYS A COMMAND-LINE STEP FOR NOW (T-398 S7, option B). scripts/onboard-franchise.ts --file --by --confirm (dry run first) is the only way to create one; no screen is built yet. Why: Ian, 2026-10-31 ("ok b"); PR #100

title: Decision 408 (2026-10-31)
text: LIPA TRIES POS V2 AND ERP V2 IN NOVEMBER, WITH TODAY'S SIGN-IN AND TODAY'S SCREENS. The minimum a store can use: Lipa only; store email + PIN sign-in (tablet pairing T-464 is not wired yet); one tablet first, then the whole store. POS v2 writes v1's Firestore format, so the ERP's 06:00 day import keeps working; the receipt bridge to Postgres starts 1 Jan. The POS v2 server is switched on with Ian on Sun 1 Nov (docs/ops/pos2-switchon-2026-11-01.md); the tablet installs pos-v2-933.apk (includes the PR #108 refund fix). Why: Ian, 2026-10-31 ("ship minimum deliverable... i want to try both this coming month", "yes lipa, go", "tomorrow morning")

title: Decision 409 (2026-10-31)
text: ONE ITEM LIST FOR EVERYTHING BOUGHT; ANY ADMIN APPROVES NEW ITEMS; SERVICES ARE ITEMS; SUB-CATEGORY LIVES ON THE ITEM (T-502). 1A: expenses use the existing items master, never a second list. 2A: any org admin (capability approve_item_request, never a manager, not the requester unless super-admin authority) approves an item request, superseding the 2026-08-28 super-admin-only rule for requests (creating, merging, renaming items stays super-admin). 3A: rent, power, water, internet are service items, never stocked. Sub-category (Ian, 1 Nov): an admin-managed list under each category, set once on the item; the cashier picks only the item; no "Please Specify"/"Other". Meat stays slab vs sliced, with dine-in/panda/retail as variations; butane is a supply. The v1 item list (258 items from 4,078 spellings) enters through an admin import screen, never a script. Why: Ian, 2026-10-31 ("1a 2a 3a") and 2026-11-01 ("yes" to sub-category on the item); docs/tasks/502-expense-item-catalog.md

title: Decision 410 (2026-11-01)
text: THE ERP SIDEBAR'S "DAILY" GROUP IS FOR EVERYDAY STORE WORK ONLY. Daily: Dashboard, Sales days, Channel settlements, Order wastage, Remittance, Till custody, Supplier invoices (recorded every day, as in v1), Expenses, Reimbursements, Cash requests. Staff, Attendance, Leave, Payroll and Government payments form a People group; set-once screens (Clock terminals, Clock lane, Payroll rates) sit in Setup; Budgets and Recurring bills in Money. A new screen joins Daily only if a store uses it every day. Why: Ian, 2026-11-01 ("yes go put invoices to daily too"); PR #110

title: Decision 430 (2026-11-06)
text: POS v2 IS A FULL-SCREEN MODULE OF THE ERP APP (/pos IN apps/erp), ON THE ONE POSTGRES, WITH THE ERP'S SIGN-IN (T-464 PAIRING + EMPLOYEE ID + PIN) AND authorize(). NO FIREBASE DATABASE, SIGN-IN OR SEPARATE POS SERVER FOR ANY NEW POS RELEASE. OFFLINE SELLING USES THE TABLET'S OWN OUTBOX (TYPED, APPEND-ONLY EVENTS KEYED (device_id, seq), POSTED TO /api/pos/events) AND A VERSIONED SNAPSHOT (/api/pos/snapshot); OTHER DEVICES POLL /api/pos/state; THE SERVER RECOMPUTES EVERY BILL AND IS THE ONLY WRITER OF TRUTH. Ian, 2026-11-06: *"lets pivot design the POS now that its backend is the same as erp like pos is a piece of erp"*, *"no firebase db now"*; then Q1 (a) "apply the rule change" and Q3 (a) "inside the ERP" on docs/plans/pos-v2-design.md. The §1, §2 rule 4 and §5 wording is brought in line with row 280 the same day. Supersedes: ADR-015 A1.1 (POS v2 in apps/pos) and A1.6 (POS server routes as a second service): apps/pos, pos2.shareat.net and the POS's app.shareat.net calls retire store by store; A2's step timing for the POS (sign-in, sales and tables become one switch per store at a business-day boundary); row 378's "P0 ships on v1's Firebase" for any release after the Lipa trial; row 275's "carrier is Firestore during P0–P1". Keeps: rows 270, 272, 276, 280, 313, 319, 351, 356, 371, 390, 391 and the §5.1 Lane A/B rules. Row 379's bridge keeps reading stores still on v1 until each switches. Clock terminals unchanged until their own task (row 280's direction stands), so the Firebas

title: Decision 431 (2026-11-06)
text: LIPA GOES LIVE ON THE NEW POS (ROW 430) ON MONDAY 7 DECEMBER 2026. THE 24-HOUR TWO-TABLET SOAK (0 LOST, 0 DOUBLED) STAYS THE GO-LIVE GATE AND RUNS BEFORE 7 DEC; IT MUST START BY WEDNESDAY 2 DEC AT THE LATEST. TO HIT THE DATE, SCOPE IS CUT, NOT PROOF. THE FIRST LIPA RELEASE IS: OPEN A STAND, ORDER (PACKAGE + À LA CARTE), REFILLS AND KITCHEN TICKETS, BILL, CASH + E-WALLET "TO CHECK", PRINT, THE OFFLINE OUTBOX AND THE SERVER RECOMPUTE, PLUS WHAT A STORE CANNOT OPEN WITHOUT (SIGN-IN, VOID OF AN UNPAID STAND, DAY CLOSE FEEDING THE ERP SALES DAY). EVERYTHING ELSE FOLLOWS AFTER GO-LIVE. Ian, 2026-11-06, Q2 (c) "rush, Lipa on the new POS by 7 Dec", chosen against the recommendation (a: keep the Firebase trial until a mid-to-late January switch) after reading the warning. The orchestrator's ruling within (c): rushing does not skip the soak, which takes one day. Lipa keeps today's trial POS v2 (row 408) until the switch, with no new features. Amends row 378 (the 7 Dec target stands, now on the new POS). Collides with row 386's "POS slices avoid merging 20 Nov–14 Dec": the build needs merges in that window. The plan merges behind a per-store switch that is off everywhere except a test store; BOSS confirms this with Ian (design §9). Slices T-522 to T-535 (design §9). Why: Discovery 42: Lipa averages 26.8 receipts a day and had 0 offline receipts in 91 days, so a small first release covers the real work; the soak is the only proof that no sale is lost or doubled

title: Decision 432 (2026-11-06)
text: LOYALTY IS NOT IN THE FIRST POS v2 RELEASE. Ian, 2026-11-06, Q4 (a). Earn and redeem are added after Lipa is stable (129 members today); they need the diner principal and the inter-org liability of row 273. Offline, loyalty is refused anyway (design §5.4). Why: Keeps the 7 Dec scope small (row 431)

title: Decision 433 (2026-11-06)
text: POS v2 SCREEN THEMES: THE KITCHEN SCREEN DEFAULTS TO GRILL NIGHT (DARK); THE TILL AND THE OTHER TABS DEFAULT TO LIGHT. A DEFAULT, CHANGEABLE PER DEVICE. Q5 was not answered; the recommended (a) is taken as the default (orchestrator, 2026-11-06). Uses the ADR-013 dark theme unchanged: light stays the ERP default, and the OS never decides. Why: A hot, bright kitchen read from a distance; mock docs/plans/pos-v2-design/kitchen-dark.png

title: Decision 434 (2026-11-06)
text: ADR-015 A8's FOUR "STILL OPEN" QUESTIONS ARE CLOSED BY LATER ROWS: Q1 business-day end → rows 348 and 390 (Z to Z); Q2 first-store date → rows 378, 408 and now 431 (7 Dec on the new POS); Q3 POS v1 feature freeze → row 348 (from 9 Nov, fixes allowed); Q4 the unsafe v1 void → row 348 (yes, DEF-651). Recorded so A8 does not read as open. Why: A decision that lived only in later rows

title: Decision 435 (2026-11-06)
text: POS v2 WORK MAY MERGE DURING 20 NOV – 14 DEC (NARROWS ROW 386), ON ONE CONDITION: THE NEW POS STAYS OFF FOR EVERY STORE, BEHIND THE PER-STORE POS SWITCH (T-523), UNTIL LIPA'S GO-LIVE (ROW 431). Ian, 2026-11-06, relayed by the orchestrator. Every merge to main is a production deploy (row 278), so /pos reaches erp2 inert: no store sees or writes through it until its switch is turned on, and turning it on is the go-live step itself (design §8). A TEST store may be switched on for the soak and the emulator. Three parallel Sonnet builder lanes are approved for weeks 2–3, each in its own worktree with its own _test database (no lane-DB-pinned tests) and no shared files. Why: Row 386's pause protected the Firebase P0 rollout; a dark switch keeps that protection while the 7 Dec build lands

title: Decision 436 (2026-11-06)
text: LIPA'S DECEMBER 2026 SALES REACH v1'S BOOKS THROUGH A WRITE-ONLY DAY-TOTAL BRIDGE (A NARROW EXCEPTION TO ROW 430), AND PRE-2027 POS ROWS IN POSTGRES ARE PURGED AT CUTOVER. Ian, 2026-11-06, option (a) of docs/plans/pos-v2-design.md §8a. After each Z, the ERP writes that day's totals for Lipa into the one Firestore document v1's sales pull reads, stores/{posStoreId}/analytics/{yyyymmdd} (payments.totalGross, txCount, byMethod, discountsTotal, chargesTotal; a full overwrite, never increments), for business dates up to 2026-12-31 only. Built inside T-531. Guards: the writer refuses any date after 31 Dec; the v2 06:00 import (T-396) skips Lipa from its switch date; the trial app is signed out at the switch so nothing else writes that document. December stock usage for Lipa is entered by hand in v1. Because v1 then holds December's booked day totals, the T-523 transactional POS tables are classed purge (row 379 confirmed for them). Why: The 2026 books close on v1 (row 379, ADR-005) and v1 reads only that document (ERP-rebuild/src/lib/server/pos-api.ts:143-168, POS/src/app/api/external/sales/route.ts:21-35); typed figures (option b) were refused as the row 270 hole, and a January go-live (option c) gave up row 431's date

title: Decision 437 (2026-11-06)
text: A SENIOR OR PWD DINER'S DISCOUNT COVERS THEIR OWN PACKAGE HEAD PLUS THE DISHES ORDERED ONLY FOR THEM; SHARED DISHES ARE NOT DISCOUNTED. Ian, 2026-11-06 (the PC-7 recommendation, after the 2024 Department of Justice opinion). The 20% discount and the VAT removal apply to that share only (PC-7 payment screen). Several qualifying diners at one table each get their own share and their own statutory_discount_records row (T-523 R12). The till marks a dish as "for" a diner when it is ordered; an unmarked dish is shared. Why: Statutory: the discount is for the qualifying person's own consumption; per-diner is what the approved payment screen shows

title: Decision 438 (2026-11-06)
text: THE POS v2 CASHIER TAKES A SPLIT PAYMENT LIKE v1: SEVERAL TENDERS ON ONE BILL (E.G. GCASH + CASH), IN RELEASE 1. ONE TABLE = ONE SALES RECEIPT; v1 HAS NO PER-PERSON SPLIT INTO SEPARATE RECEIPTS AND NO PAY-LATER, SO NEITHER IS BUILT. Ian, 2026-11-06: *"cashier payment screen must process split payment like v1"*. v1's goal (§1.2d): the diner pays with whatever mix they carry, the cashier sees the balance shrink with each tender, change comes only from cash, and the drawer and wallet totals stay right. v1's method (POS/src/components/cashier/payment-modal.tsx:271-279, 720-737; lib/checkout/receipt-math.ts:59-75; lib/server/pos-commands/checkout.ts:111): a "Split Payment" button adds a row with the remaining balance pre-filled; a reference is required where the method has one; overpaying is allowed only if cash covers the change; at most 20 tenders; the receipt stores a map keyed by method NAME (same names merged) and prints one line per tender, then CHANGE; references are not printed. v2 keeps the behaviour and beats the method: one pos_sales_receipt_payments row per tender keyed by tender_id (T-523 R8), never by name; exact centavos (no 1-centavo tolerance needed); each tender's reference is stored on its row and printed on the receipt so the wallet can be matched; offline, an e-wallet tender is "to check" (A3); at most 20 tenders per sales receipt (T-524 rule). Mock: docs/plans/pos-v2-design/payment.png. Why: A split was the one part of v1's payment screen release 1 would othe

title: Decision 439 (2026-11-06)
text: THE POS v2 BILL AND SALES RECEIPT ARE ITEMIZED, ONE LINE PER PACKAGE AND PER À LA CARTE ITEM (QTY × UNIT PRICE = GROSS, ITS DISCOUNTS, LINE NET), AND A DISCOUNT ATTACHES TO A LINE AND COVERS SOME OR ALL OF ITS UNITS, AS IN v1. SENIOR/PWD USES THE SAME PER-LINE MODEL: THE DINER'S OWN HEAD IS ONE UNIT OF THE PACKAGE LINE AND A DISH ORDERED ONLY FOR THEM IS UNITS OF ITS LINE (ROW 437). IN RELEASE 1. Ian, 2026-11-06: *"wont ala carte be itemized in billing? i suggest per item line with discount like v1 does"*. v1's goal (§1.2d): a discount, a free item or a senior's share is visible on the exact dish it applies to. v1's method (POS/src/lib/types.ts:705-748, lib/tax.ts:95-160, components/cashier/edit-billable-item-dialog.tsx:409-427): a lineAdjustments map per bill line (preset or custom, % or ₱ per unit, qty covered, oldest first); SC/PWD only as a whole-bill discount; no role check on a line discount; the print shows qty, item, gross and an unnamed "Discount (Nx)". v2 keeps the behaviour and beats the method: discount presets become ERP master data (pos_discount_presets, T-523 R13; Lipa's six are loaded from v1, the editing screen is T-535); senior/PWD is per line and per diner, with one statutory record per diner; a unit covered by senior/PWD carries no other discount (the statute gives the 20%, not 20% plus a promo; v1 stacked them); the receipt prints the unit price, each discount's name, and the line net. Open for Ian: who may give a discount (recommended: a preset by the ca

title: Decision 440 (2026-11-06)
text: ANY CASHIER MAY GIVE ANY LINE DISCOUNT, A PRESET OR A TYPED ₱ OR %, WITH NO MANAGER PIN (AS v1); EVERY LINE DISCOUNT RECORDS WHO APPLIED IT, WHEN, AND (IF REMOVED) WHO REMOVED IT. NO WHOLE-BILL DISCOUNT IN RELEASE 1: A TABLE PROMO IS ONE PRESET APPLIED TO EVERY LINE WITH AN "APPLY TO ALL" TAP. Ian, 2026-11-06, answering the two open items of row 439; (1) is against the recommendation (a manager PIN for a typed discount). Audit is the control: table_session_line_discounts.applied_by / removed_by and the frozen receipt copy (T-523 R13); a report of typed discounts by cashier is a later slice. approved_by stays in the schema, unused, so a PIN can be switched on later without a migration. Why: Matches how Lipa works today; the audit trail replaces the PIN

title: Decision 441 (2026-11-03)
text: MENU DAYPARTS ARE BUILT NOW, AND A PACKAGE SOLD AT DIFFERENT PRICES AT LUNCH AND DINNER IS ONE PACKAGE WITH TWO DAYPART OFFERS, NOT TWO PACKAGES (v1'S "LT-" AND "DT-" COPIES). Ian, 2026-11-03: *"yes add daypart NOW"*, then chose one package with two daypart offers. v1's goal (§1.2d): a cashier can only start or change to a package whose time window is open, at the price of that window. Design: menu_dayparts (store, name, days, start, end in the store's own timezone; overnight windows belong to the day they start; start inclusive, end exclusive) and menu_offers.daypart_id (null = all day); a variant may not hold an all-day and a dayparted live offer together, and windows may not overlap; an invalid state means NOT OFFERED, never a fallback price (migration 0233, T-510 S1a, PR #148). A table started at 16:55 keeps its lunch price (R5). The business day (starts 05:00) and the dayparts (price) are separate things (R7). Spec docs/tasks/510-menu-dayparts.md. Why: One item, one recipe, one report line, and a price change is one new offer; v1's two copies drifted apart

title: Decision 442 (2026-11-05)
text: THE FIVE LUNCH/DINNER PACKAGE PAIRS ARE CONFIRMED, WHERE LUNCH AND DINNER COST THE SAME THE PACKAGE IS ONE ALL-DAY OFFER, DAVAO "PORK PREMIUM" IS LUNCH-ONLY, THE FOUR DISABLED PACKAGES ARE NOT LOADED, AND A SUPER ADMIN CAN CHANGE ANY PAIRING AFTERWARDS IN THE ERP. Ian, 2026-11-05, answering the pairing table: *"1 yes but i want to have the ability to modify it as super admin / 2 a / 3 a / 4 yes"*. (1) Pairs: Pork and Chicken, Pork and Beef, Chicken and Beef, Triple Feast, Seafood Cruise (v1's DT_Pork and Beef is a typo of DT-Pork and Beef). (2) One all-day offer where lunch = dinner: Pork and Chicken at Lipa and Malvar, all five pairs at Davao. (3) Davao Pork Premium (258): one package in the lunch window (11:00-17:00), no dinner offer. (4) Valentine Promo, Valentine Promo 2 (Lipa, Malvar), Davao "Beef" and "Pork Regular" are not loaded. Bundles (Barkada, Squad, VIP, VIP 2, VIP PARTY) have no window in v1 and load all-day. The loading itself (S5) is deferred, see row 445. Why: A price that is the same twice is one number to change later; the signed table avoids guessing from inconsistent v1 names

title: Decision 443 (2026-11-05)
text: A STORE'S LUNCH AND DINNER HOURS ARE EDITED BY ADMINS AND BY THAT STORE'S OWN MANAGERS (manage_store_settings); ONLY THE PAIRING OF AN OFFER TO A DAYPART IS SUPER ADMIN (pair_menu_dayparts); MANAGERS STILL RE-PRICE AN EXISTING WINDOW (set_menu_price, row 316). THE HOURS DIFFER PER STORE. Ian, 2026-11-05, answering who edits a store's hours: *"a"*. Windows: Lipa 08:00-17:00 / 17:00-08:00; Malvar 01:00-17:00 / 17:00-01:00; Davao 11:00-17:00 / 17:00-23:00; all seven days. pair_menu_dayparts covers creating a pairing, re-linking an offer, switching to all-day, and withdrawing a daypart slot; it is granted to the owner (migration 0234, T-510 S2, PR #153). Screens: /admin/stores/[id] (admins) and /menu/hours (managers), plus the When select and per-window prices on /menu/prices (S3, PR #158). Why: Hours are a store-level business setting a manager knows best; pairing changes the menu's structure and is the owner's

title: Decision 444 (2026-11-05)
text: NO BUSINESS SETTING IS HARD-CODED ANYWHERE IN THE ERP: EVERY BUSINESS VALUE (A PRICE PAIRING, A TIME WINDOW, A RATE, A LIMIT, A TOLERANCE) LIVES IN THE DATABASE WITH AN ERP SCREEN TO CHANGE IT, THE RIGHT CAPABILITY, AND AN AUDIT TRAIL. CODE CONSTANTS ARE ONLY FILE-FORMAT FACTS AND VALUES FIXED BY LAW, AND EVEN A LEGAL RATE GOES IN A SETTINGS TABLE WITH AN EFFECTIVE DATE IF IT CAN CHANGE. Ian, 2026-11-05: *"again nothing in this erp system like this business settings must not be hard coded, must always have a ui door to manage them"* ("again": 2026-11-03, about kitchen stations, *"there must be a ui door on erp for this"*). Every spec review asks which values are business settings; a spec or PR that hard-codes one is rejected. Structure is super admin, a store's own prices and hours are its manager (rows 316, 443). The generic settings table is T-511 S5c. Why: The owner runs the business from the ERP; a value only a developer can change blocks him and drifts from reality

title: Decision 445 (2026-11-06)
text: THE TABLET RESOLVES THE LUNCH OR DINNER PRICE ITSELF, EVEN OFFLINE; REFILLS ARE NOT TIED TO HOURS; AND THE v1 MENU IMPORT AND T-510 S5 (LOADING THE HOURS AND PAIRINGS) COME AFTER THE OPEN WORKTREES ARE CLEAN, AS THEIR OWN TASK. Ian's standing order (2026-11-05, via BOSS): finish every open worktree, new task only when all is clean. (1) Projection: StoreMenuV2 is extended additively (no V3): nextChangeAt includes the next hours boundary and a closed package shows outside_hours with the time it opens (S4, PR #163); the menu carries hours and per-variant slots and the tablet picks the open window from its cached menu with a pure copy of the window logic, kept honest by a parity test, so it flips at 17:00 with no network (S4b, PR #167). (2) Refills and flavours are not window-gated (v1 never read refill windows, and a running table keeps refilling after its window closes). (3) Defect found: the APK's menu GET was blocked by CORS (T-508 S5); fixed in S4b. (4) Deferred: no v1 menu loader exists (spec 401 defers the import), so the menu import is its own task after cleanup, and T-510 S5 only attaches dayparts and pairings to it (rows 441-443 stay valid). The tablet test at Lipa is still owed; Lipa's 7 December launch stays on the v1 menu (T-508 R9 blocks any store from the ERP menu until then). Why: A phone or tablet with a bad signal must still charge the right price; importing the whole v1 menu is a larger decision than attaching hours

title: Decision 446 (2026-11-07)
text: NO POSITION PICKER IN POS RELEASE 1: A PERSON WITH TWO POSITIONS ACTS WITH ALL THEIR GRANTS, AS IN THE ERP TODAY. ROW 323'S "PICK ONE AFTER THE PIN, THE PICK ONLY NARROWS" STAYS THE TARGET, AFTER RELEASE 1. Ian, 2026-11-07, via BOSS, answering T-526 Open O1. acting_position_id is not implemented anywhere (apps/, packages/), and building it would delay Lipa's 7 Dec go-live (row 431). The server still checks every action with authorize(), and the offline tablet only greys out buttons from the snapshot's posCapabilities (T-526 R5). Why: Row 323's narrowing is a refinement; release 1 behaves exactly like the ERP a person already uses

title: Decision 447 (2026-11-07)
text: IN POS RELEASE 1, SERVERS DO NOT ADD DISHES FROM THEIR PHONES. THE CASHIER ENTERS EVERY ORDER ON THE STORE TABLET; A SERVER'S PHONE DOES REFILLS AND HEAD CONFIRMATION ONLY. ON A PHONE OR KITCHEN BROWSER THE ORDERS TAB IS READ-ONLY. Ian, 2026-11-07, via BOSS, answering T-527 Open O1. Server and Kitchen positions hold no record_sale (0240 defaults), and phones have no outbox (T-525 is tablet-only). Adding dishes from a phone would need a new capability and a second online write path. At Lipa the cashier already enters every order on the one billing tablet (row 313). Why: Keeps one write path (the tablet outbox) for every order in release 1; the phone path can be added later with its own capability

title: Decision 448 (2026-11-07)
text: EVERY POS STAND-NUMBER PICKER IS ONE HORIZONTAL ROW THAT SLIDES SIDEWAYS (SWIPE, SCROLL-SNAP, TARGETS OF AT LEAST 48 PX, THE SELECTED STAND SCROLLED INTO VIEW, ARROW KEYS MOVE ALONG IT). IT NEVER WRAPS OR SQUEEZES INTO A GRID, HOWEVER MANY STANDS A STORE HAS. Ian, 2026-11-07, via BOSS: *"try stand number that is more than 12 it must not cramp all numbers at the top it must slide using 1 row only"*. Stands are tapped, never typed (row 371). A store with more than 12 stands must not lose the screen to a grid of numbers. Built in T-528 (Addendum 2), and tested with 30 stands. Why: Keeps the seat panel's content (heads, items, Items so far) on screen at any store size

title: Decision 449 (2026-11-07)
text: A SALES DAY DERIVED FROM POS v2 RECEIPTS (source = 'pos_receipts') IS VERIFIED ONLY BY A STORE MANAGER OR ABOVE (BY ROLE) WHO HOLDS verify_sales_day AT THAT STORE AND DID NOT CLOSE THE Z. verify_own_sales_day DOES NOT EXEMPT. v1-FED AND TYPED DAYS KEEP TODAY'S RULE. Ian, 2026-11-07, via BOSS, answering T-531 O1. The Z already has a cashier's close and a manager's PIN approval. The verification that posts the day to the ledger is a third, senior pair of eyes on the cash. Spec: T-531 R10. Why: Stricter control only where the new POS creates the figures; nothing changes for the v1 feed during the switch

title: Decision 450 (2026-11-07)
text: A POS v2 Z THAT WOULD COVER MORE THAN 2 BUSINESS DAYS IS REFUSED WITH "CALL A MANAGER". THE MANAGER THEN RUNS "CLOSE DAY BY DAY" WITH THEIR PIN: ONE Z AND ONE SALES DAY PER PAST BUSINESS DAY THAT HAS SALES, OLDEST FIRST, WITH TODAY LEFT OPEN. IT IS AUDITED AS ONE BACKLOG CLOSE. Ian, 2026-11-07, via BOSS, answering T-531 O2. A forgotten Z covering 2 dates stays allowed (row 390). Longer gaps would book several days of sales on one date, so they are split by the receipts' own business dates. Spec: T-531 R11. Why: Keeps every day's sales on its own date even after a missed close

title: Decision 451 (2026-11-08)
text: SAVE IS A FLOPPY DISK. VERIFY AND CONFIRM ARE A CHECK. A PERIOD CLOSE ("CLOSE MONTH / BRANCH / SHIFT ...") IS A PADLOCK, NEVER THE CANCEL X. APPROVE IS A THUMBS-UP. POST (TO THE LEDGER) IS A BOOK. EVERY OTHER ICON IS UNCHANGED UNTIL IAN RULES AGAIN. Ian, 2026-11-08, via BOSS, after seeing the icon-only button grid (T-549). Submit and Send keep the paper plane; a bare "Close", Cancel, Discard and Dismiss keep the X. Spec: docs/tasks/549-save-and-verify-icons.md. Why: A cancel X on a month close read as "cancel", and one paper plane for approve, post and verify hid which step you are taking

title: Decision 452 (2026-11-08)
text: v1 AND v2 ARE SEPARATE BACKENDS EXCEPT SIGN-IN (AUTH) AND FILE STORAGE. A STORE ON POS v1 STAYS ON THE v1 ERP (ITS BOOKS AND ITS STOCK) UNTIL IT SWITCHES TO POS v2; THE v2 ERP COVERS ONLY STORES ON POS v2, FROM EACH STORE'S SWITCH DATE. "POS USAGE PULL" AND "POS ITEM MAPPING" ARE RETIRED NOW. SUPERSEDES ROW 379's NIGHTLY v1-RECEIPT BRIDGE INTO POSTGRES FOR ALL STORES FROM 1 JAN 2027. Ian, 2026-11-08, via BOSS: *"the plan is completely separate backend for v1 and v2, except auth and storage, so pulling v1's records like that mapping to v2 won't pay off since v2 will have a shared backend."* What it supersedes: row 379 parts (2) and (3) as they apply to v1 stores (the nightly per-receipt bridge for all stores; the T-396 extension); rows 341–342 (the v1-pull usage drafts and their auto-post); and any plan that books v1 stores in the v2 ERP from 2027 (ADR-005's single opening on 1 Jan for every store; docs/plans/pos-customer-v2-phase-plan.md and pos-v2-design.md §3.1 "Nightly receipt bridge"). Still standing: row 436, the December day-total bridge from POS v2 to v1 for Lipa (T-531). It writes into v1 so that v1's 2026 books stay whole, and it is not a v1→v2 import. Consequences: (1) the 2026 and 2027 books are split per store by switch date. Lipa is on the v2 ERP from 7 Dec 2026 (but its 2026 books still close on v1, through the December bridge). Malvar, Davao and Padre Garcia stay on the v1 ERP until each switches in 2027. (2) Reports that cover all stores need v1 + v2 consolida

title: Decision 453 (2026-11-11)
text: A POS v2 SALE WHOSE PAYMENT IS A LITTLE SHORT OF THE SERVER'S RECOMPUTED TOTAL IS RECORDED, NEVER REFUSED OR QUARANTINED. THE GAP IS FLAGGED AS A VARIANCE. THE TOLERANCE IS A BUSINESS RULE, pos.sale_variance_tolerance: DEFAULT ₱0.01, EDITABLE BY AN ADMIN, HARD MAXIMUM ₱0.10. A GAP ABOVE THE TOLERANCE IS STILL RECORDED, AND IS FLAGGED AS A FINDING, NOT REFUSED. Ian, 2026-11-11, via BOSS, answering audit item P-002.
